scope.summary: Partial reconstruction of Level-0 definitions and scoped physical, chemical, biochemical, cellular, optical, retinal, visual and neural evidence. Levels organize the display; they do not establish a universal emergence order. Formal specifications, computational models, experimental preparations, observations and conditional interpretations have distinct roles. Each scientific claim retains its reviewed sources, selected system, observable, uncertainty, shared inputs and unresolved limitations. Field and particle models remain distinct from detector response, lattice calculations and conditional parameter extraction. Nuclear and atomic masses, primordial abundances and cosmological spectra retain their source-specific calibration, model and covariance limits. Atomic and molecular binding, prepared-state spectroscopy, charge production, electrolyte screening and stationary electronic representations address different questions; their energy comparisons do not by themselves establish formation kinetics, universal stability or a unique ancestry. Optical and neural records distinguish measured response from anatomy, intervention and theoretical interpretation. Cellular organization, state regulation, fate and immune responses retain preparation-specific perturbations, finite persistence, partial rescue, contrary outcomes and corrected controls. Model-derived metabolic flux and inferred immune networks remain distinct from measured readouts. Behavioral success and fitted models do not identify a unique mechanism. Finite checks reproduce only their declared data or mathematical witnesses, not entire experiments. Cross-domain construction, universal parent weights and carrier minima, downward causation and a derivation of quantum theory from Level 0 remain unestablished. Source discrepancies and unreproduced stages remain explicit. No whole-graph scientific validation is claimed.
scope.levelInterpretation: Display groups inherited from the catalogue; no universal hierarchy, developmental order or derivation from Level 0 is inferred.

sources.title: MAMI elastic cross-section ratio table

locators: arXiv:1307.6227v2 archive member aux/CrossSections/CrossSections.dat: complete author table, interpreted with aux/explanation.pdf
review.limit: The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input. The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. The 315-MeV acquisition uses the current-based luminosity estimate after a monitor-setting problem. Kinematics must use the acceptance-averaged Q^2 and beam energy, not the central spectrometer angle. Multiplying columns 5-8 by column 9 undoes the applied Coulomb correction. Columns 12-18 change model normalization; the systematic variations in column 10 require new fits, not new observations.

review.limit: Rosenbluth separation reuses the spline-fit normalization and projects the same finite-acceptance data to 77 Q^2 values. Its 77 unconstrained pairs and four additional low-Q^2 constrained alternatives are not independent data sets. The latter impose GM/(mu_p*G_dipole) at 1 and 1.05; their GE alternatives are not an ordinary confidence interval. Rosenbluth.dat stores GM, whereas the selected spline file stores GM/mu_p. The unconstrained Rosenbluth uncertainties are statistical; no complete cross-point or GE-GM covariance is supplied by these selected files.

limitations: Bilateral hippocampal antisense injections reduce the named transporter in tissue. They are not genetically restricted to a cell class. Astrocytic MCT4 and neuronal MCT2 attribution uses expression evidence; direct cell-to-cell lactate flux was not measured in these behavioral assays.

limitations: Male Cx3cr1-EGFP/+ mice received thalamic viral labeling and hM3Dq; imaging was performed five weeks later in primary motor cortex, 100-150 micrometers below the surface. This is separate from striatal neuronal calcium imaging.

Figure 3h specifies intraperitoneal CNO and clopidogrel, while the imaging Methods states intravenous CNO. The route is unresolved. The caption describes a 1 square-micrometer region, while Methods specifies a 2-micrometer-diameter bouton ROI; no calibrated contact-area estimate is adopted.

Bouton-localized fluorescence and process-tip motion are morphological proxies. They do not directly measure extracellular ATP, synaptic strength or neuronal suppression. Tips and cells are nested within mice; systemic pharmacology does not establish absolute microglia specificity.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

limitations: Wild-type C57BL/6J experiments use male mice aged three to four months. Genetic cohorts include males and females pooled after reported baseline comparisons; experimenters were blinded to genotype only. The stated birth-order randomization and counterbalancing do not specify the random sequence. Grubbs outlier exclusions and a greater-than-five-percent initial hyperemia inclusion rule are reported without a complete included/excluded-animal manifest.

The ATP-depletion assay uses mixed microvessel lysates, including endothelial cells, distal pericytes and astrocyte endfeet. Residual ATP is an inverse kinase-activity proxy under added substrate/cofactors, not direct membrane PIP2 concentration. GTPgammaS is not selective for Arf6. Results give 0.012% DMSO whereas Methods give 0.01%; exact solvent concentration needs resolution.

NAV-2729 is pharmacological and not exclusively Arf6-selective. Main Methods describe additional GEF/GAP targets in overlapping concentration ranges. Genetic comparisons and supplementation constrain interpretation but do not identify a unique PIP2-mediated route or exclude effects in other neurovascular cells.

Separate supporting information, animal identifiers, raw recordings and analysis code remain unread or unavailable here. Main Figures 1-4 and Methods support scoped reported outcomes, not independent reproduction of data, exclusions, nesting or statistics. Supplemental genotype, blood-pressure, glucose and lower-dose controls are not independently admitted.

PIP2 availability is inferred from kinase and Kir current assays; the study does not directly quantify membrane lipid abundance or test all Arf6 pathways. Cross-preparation consistency does not prove that this is the sole mediator of blood-flow responses or a universal rule for constructing the graph.

limitations: Adult mice of both sexes, overall age range 8-41 weeks. BMX:CreERT2 Gja4fl/fl Gja5fl/fl animals and Cre-negative double-floxed controls both receive tamoxifen. The driver targets arterial endothelium beyond the brain, including aorta; it is not a capillary-only or brain-only intervention. Assay-specific age/sex distributions are not fully resolved.

No prospective sample-size calculation. Genotype-blinded functional imaging acquisition and randomized stimulus order are reported; random stimulus order is not random genotype allocation. Pre-unblinding exclusions lack a complete animal manifest. The Gja4 floxed allele has an oocyte hypomorphism; same-flox controls do not establish equivalence to wild-type physiology.

Aortic electrophysiology uses six cells from only two mice per genotype; tracer loading uses six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype. Cell-level tests do not supply six or eight independent animals. Apparent capacitance includes the coupled network, not just one cell surface. These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

PMC author-manuscript passages and the author-hosted in-press PDF were read, including main Figures 1-6 and supplementary Figures S5-S7. Selected Methods cover the admitted assays; general cloning/culture methods and remaining supplemental material were not fully audited. Final bibliographic pagination is 5003-5019.e22, whereas the read in-press PDF ends its Methods at e12; version completeness remains unresolved.

Separate statistical/genotyping Tables S1-S2, allele-map files and movies were not obtained or replayed. Raw measurements are available from the authors on request and have not been obtained. The paper identifies code DOI 10.7910/DVN/XRRGRI, but public repository access failed; code files were not inspected or executed. No numerical edge weights or independent experimental reproduction are claimed.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

Specific rat learning protocols alter retained birth labels; a separate macaque study supplies age-limited neuronal colabels. Neither establishes a universal learning prerequisite or a selective newborn-neuron requirement for memory.

Rakic (1985) and Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) propose that stable neurons preserve learned information. Their autoradiographic nulls contain no matched memory test and appear to share specimens. This proposed stability mechanism and later renewal-benefit hypotheses are not adjudicated by histology alone.

Pattern separation, temporal context and memory resolution remain nonexclusive interpretations. Behavioral discrimination, population-code decorrelation and temporal association require different measurements; review schematics cannot choose among them.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

limitations: Five cancer patients received diagnostic BrdU labeling; one patient with similar cancer and no BrdU served as a staining control. This is an observational autopsy series, not a randomized intervention on neurogenesis or a healthy-population survey.

A single intravenous infusion contained 250 mg BrdU in 100 ml saline. No anticancer therapy was given before or during labeling and no cerebral metastases were found at autopsy. BrdU marks DNA synthesis and subsequent label retention. The neuronal-marker interpretation supports candidate adult-born cells under the labeling assumptions; the images do not continuously observe cell division, trace a clone or selectively exclude every nonmitotic DNA-synthesis mechanism.

NeuN, NSE and calbindin were alternative neuronal stains with BrdU and GFAP, not three independent birthdating assays or necessarily three labels on each same cell. Reported neuronal percentages use BrdU-positive cells as denominator, not all neurons. At least twenty BrdU-positive cells per patient were examined; exact marker-specific denominators and patient-level counts are unavailable.

BrdU/GFAP-positive cells and cells lacking the selected phenotype markers were also observed. Marker-negative cells cannot be assigned automatically to a quiescent stem-cell lineage, and fractions from different marker assays cannot be added as disjoint cell classes.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

limitations: The accepted supplement starts with 156 fractions (74 NeuN-positive and 82 NeuN-negative), retains 55 and 65 for isotope analysis, and uses 51 and 64 for individual 2POP fits after four neuronal and one nonneuronal exclusions. Paired analyses use 40 pairs. These are different analysis populations, not 120 independent donors.

This is an observational autopsy study, not a randomized neurogenesis intervention. Main text gives ages 19-92, but accepted Table S1 includes NeuN-negative pub_id 53 aged 16.2. Table S1 also contains pre-2000 death dates despite the stated 2000-2012 tissue procurement interval. Donor identity, procurement chronology, clinical selection, exclusions and the final sample manifest need reconciliation.

Accepted Table S1 gives different birth-date/age entries for the two fractions labeled pub_id 49, while neuronal pub_id 69 and nonneuronal pub_id 68 share displayed age, birth/death dates and sex. Neither identical metadata nor matching pub_id alone establishes the complete paired donor manifest.

AMS measures bulk genomic-DNA carbon-14, reported as fraction modern or decay-corrected delta carbon-14. These are isotope concentrations, not counts of new neurons or single-cell birth timestamps. The method integrates DNA synthesis under assumptions about atmospheric carbon and the food chain.

NeuN sorting separates marker-positive nuclei from a heterogeneous marker-negative fraction, which includes several glial and vascular-associated cell types. Representative Figure S1 purities are not the purity of every sample; Table S1 includes neuronal sorting purity of 79%. Linear mixture correction does not independently validate cell lineage, and nonneuronal NA fields are not zero contamination.

AMS was blinded to sample age and origin. This does not establish blinding of all collection, selection or modeling. The main instrumental error description does not replace the sample-specific SD columns. Accepted Table S1 includes unresolved SD entries, such as F14C SD 1.01 alongside delta carbon-14 SD 14.00 for neuronal pub_id 21; values have not been silently corrected.

The birthdating interpretation assumes stable DNA after the last division and new cells arising from an actively proliferating progenitor pool. DNA synthesis is not a continuously observed division or clone. An old postmitotic reservoir migrating into the tissue was not modeled; the discussion of DNA repair includes unpublished stroke observations and does not selectively test every alternative.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

limitations: The accepted supplement starts with 156 fractions (74 NeuN-positive and 82 NeuN-negative), retains 55 and 65 for isotope analysis, and uses 51 and 64 for individual 2POP fits after four neuronal and one nonneuronal exclusions. Paired analyses use 40 pairs. These are different analysis populations, not 120 independent donors.

Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

limitations: Eighteen rhesus monkeys span E140 to seventeen years: seventeen receive autoradiography and one E144 animal is used only for electron-microscopic GFAP. Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. This is evidence of overlapping material, pending original identity confirmation. Shared juvenile identifiers also have discordant age/survival reporting: 030783 is P149-P184 here versus seven months at death in 1985; 031683 is P507-P549 and six weeks here versus nineteen months and thirty-five days. Neither independent pooling nor silent record merging is justified.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

GFAP immunochemistry uses 30-micrometre vibratome sections from five animals. Antibody penetration reaches only about three micrometres. The normal-goat-serum primary-antibody control is incubated at 4 degrees C, whereas primary antiserum incubation is at room temperature. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

The P149-P184 interval is thirty-five days/five weeks in Table 1 and text, but Figure 4B says six weeks. Figure 5 uses P507-P549. Neither is an adult cohort. The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

limitations: The fit uses selected sequences and group error profiles, with fixed capacity Kmax=12 and chosen noise assumptions. Fitted probabilities combine within-person nonuse and between-person variation; they are not measured fractions of people lacking a resource. No held-out task or neural carrier test is reported.

The printed implementation is not unambiguous: S1 Text gives three repetitions of a two-output program an eight-output example; with binary logarithms its listed Repeat+1 program costs 7 while the figure labels K=5. Main-text 2points/4points costs are 6/9, whereas S1 Figure 2 labels 7/11. The formula, initial-state convention and program inventory require reconciliation before exact minima are admitted.

The reduced-resource description sets disallowed program costs to 12 while the stated threshold admits costs at most 12. Prefix correction, random-choice indexing and selection among programs versus sequences also require reconciliation. Published plots alone do not resolve these choices.

The 2021 MEG supplement repeats the cost-5 repeat description and lists an initial output followed by four pairs for alternate and two-crosses sequences. These descriptions require consistent output-length and cost conventions before executable or minimum-program claims.

Wang et al. (2019) uses alternating two-step and opposing one-step rotations, while Al Roumi et al. (2021) uses three-step and opposing one-step rotations under the same alternate name. Two-crosses is treated as three-level in 2019 and non-nested in the 2021 table. Template identity and parse must be explicit; names do not determine a shared structure.

claims.statement: The published model represents variable use of point symmetry and nested loops through fitted availability probabilities. This can describe selected group error profiles, but it does not uniquely identify which individuals possess a resource or why they fail to use it. In the Munduruku fit, full nesting with reduced point-symmetry use performs comparably to the two-resource fit.

claims.statement: For a nonzero target displacement, Wang et al. define anticipation index as gaze-to-current-target distance at target onset divided by previous-to-current-target distance. Zero means gaze at the upcoming target; gaze at the previous target gives one, although other gaze positions can also give one. Lower values indicate greater anticipation. This ratio is not the percentage of anticipatory movements and is not generally bounded above by one.

limitations: Pion, kaon and Xi are inputs in the Xi set; pion, kaon and Omega are inputs in the Omega set. The twelve channels yield nine predictions per set. Both sets reuse the same ensembles and do not independently replicate one another.

The mass and continuum extrapolations are correlated. Two normalization methods, two chiral/Taylor strategies, three pion-mass ranges, two continuum forms linear in a or a^2, and eighteen time windows produce 432 analysis variants per hadron in each normalization set, not 432 experiments.

The central value is the fit-quality-weighted distribution median. The central 68% interval of that variant distribution estimates systematic uncertainty; 2000 bootstrap datasets supply the median distribution and its central 68% statistical interval. Statistical and systematic errors are combined in quadrature for final plotted bars.

The fit family estimates selected extrapolation and excited-state effects. Exact fit-quality weights, raw correlators, full covariances and independent fit replay are unavailable here; the paper's description of blind analysis does not establish a separately audited outcome-masking protocol.

Finite-volume image corrections use M_X(L)=M_X+c_X(M_pi)*exp(-M_pi*L)/(M_pi*L)^(3/2), with volume scans at about a=0.125 fm and M_pi=320 MeV. Resonance corrections additionally use a scattering model; no precise width determination is supplied.

The lightest pion-mass point at a about 0.085 fm is excluded for rho and Delta because the lowest level is dominated by a two-particle state and weakly sensitive to the resonance mass. All other mass-range cuts remain part of the analysis.

Table S2 fractions are correlated, non-Gaussian and averaged across Xi/Omega sets. Finite-volume terms are treated as corrections. The fractions must not be summed or normalized as independent probabilities or independent variances.

The comparison uses the paper's PDG 2006 isospin averages. QED and isospin breaking are absent; leading pion/kaon electromagnetic adjustments and the neglected residual effects remain approximations. The result does not resolve the proton-neutron mass difference.

A mass spectrum does not establish stability against weak decay, a neutron lifetime, a real-time hadron formation path, a universal three-constituent minimum, nuclear stability or downward causation. The introductory percentages about visible matter and mass origin are not calculated decompositions in this study.

Figure 3 shaded bands represent experimental decay widths, not mass-measurement uncertainties. Input symbols have no error bars because their values set model parameters; this is not evidence of exact independent prediction.

The aluminum-exposed subset accounts for about 34% of the combined 2017/2018 data, not 34% of every year. The reported material-loss correction must remain part of the final lifetime interpretation.

limitations: The production data are from trapdoor-loaded UCN in 2020, 2021 and 2022. This paper reports a 45 cm/about 45 neV trap depth and cleaning at 38 cm; those numbers must not silently replace the different 2017/2018 preparation description.

Typical loading lasts 300 s, followed by 50 s cleaning. Storage octets use 20,1550,1550,50,100,1550,1550,200 s; surviving-neutron readout first probes cleaning height, then lowers the dagger to about 1 cm above the bottom. Diagnostic timing differs.

Roundhouse-dump normalization and a second, energy-sensitive monitor reduce sensitivity to the loaded spectrum; they do not make its distribution identical to the stored population. Short-hold data fit spectral and rolling normalization corrections.

Coincidences begin with two PMTs within 100 ns, extend until a gap above 1000 ns and use a 20 ns fixed dead time; the standard threshold is ten photons. Detector-live-time and photon-tail/pileup corrections are fitted or simulated, not independently replayed here.

About 90% of production runs pass analyzer-dependent selection. At least three analyses per year share the acquisitions. Timing was blinded with factors 0.99986-1.00171, but wrongly rejected 2020 runs were restored after unblinding; the reported change to the 2020-2022 combination is about -0.14 s. Final selection must not be described as entirely blinded.

Equation 2 uses an empirically scaled yield-error model with DQE factors, including a net-count rather than independent peak-plus-background variance term. DQE parameters are adjusted from short-hold fluctuations and fit quality; reduced chi-square one is partly imposed, not an independent validation of the noise model.

Rolling normalization uses short holds in overlapping blocks, typically fifteen runs within epochs. Its covariance and uncertainty are not independently reconstructed by dividing a printed yield error by the fitted correction factor.
No acquisition-to-event selection, monitor correction, full covariance, Monte Carlo correction or lifetime-fit replay is supplied by this graph.
The post-unblinding restoration concerns a roughly 659-run subset in 2020 with a reported 1.0 s lifetime shift. This is a selection correction, not a new independent experiment.

limitations: The production data are from trapdoor-loaded UCN in 2020, 2021 and 2022. This paper reports a 45 cm/about 45 neV trap depth and cleaning at 38 cm; those numbers must not silently replace the different 2017/2018 preparation description.

Typical loading lasts 300 s, followed by 50 s cleaning. Storage octets use 20,1550,1550,50,100,1550,1550,200 s; surviving-neutron readout first probes cleaning height, then lowers the dagger to about 1 cm above the bottom. Diagnostic timing differs.

Roundhouse-dump normalization and a second, energy-sensitive monitor reduce sensitivity to the loaded spectrum; they do not make its distribution identical to the stored population. Short-hold data fit spectral and rolling normalization corrections.

Coincidences begin with two PMTs within 100 ns, extend until a gap above 1000 ns and use a 20 ns fixed dead time; the standard threshold is ten photons. Detector-live-time and photon-tail/pileup corrections are fitted or simulated, not independently replayed here.

About 90% of production runs pass analyzer-dependent selection. At least three analyses per year share the acquisitions. Timing was blinded with factors 0.99986-1.00171, but wrongly rejected 2020 runs were restored after unblinding; the reported change to the 2020-2022 combination is about -0.14 s. Final selection must not be described as entirely blinded.

Equation 2 uses an empirically scaled yield-error model with DQE factors, including a net-count rather than independent peak-plus-background variance term. DQE parameters are adjusted from short-hold fluctuations and fit quality; reduced chi-square one is partly imposed, not an independent validation of the noise model.

Rolling normalization uses short holds in overlapping blocks, typically fifteen runs within epochs. Its covariance and uncertainty are not independently reconstructed by dividing a printed yield error by the fitted correction factor.
No acquisition-to-event selection, monitor correction, full covariance, Monte Carlo correction or lifetime-fit replay is supplied by this graph.
Strip results and gain-reweighted fits use the same stored-neutron sample. They diagnose readout sensitivity; they do not define four neutron species or four independent lifetime experiments.

limitations: These four runs are a subset of the 14 charged production ensembles, not an independent replication of the 41-ensemble result. The temporal extent changes with the spatial box and the QED_L large-time assumptions remain applicable.

The bare coupling e=1.00 is larger than the physical coupling. Figure 1 uses the approximate label bare alpha about 1/10; e^2/(4*pi), the renormalized flow coupling and physical alpha are distinct quantities.
The plotted kaon mass-squared difference is negative at this enhanced coupling. That sign is not the physical kaon mass ordering and is not evidence of a neutron-proton sign reversal.

No significant neutral-kaon volume dependence is resolved in this scan; that does not prove exactly zero corrections. The charged-neutral difference needs a fitted 1/L^3 term in addition to the universal leading terms.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

The 1999 inverse-meter conversions are 1.331025045(11)e-15 u and 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. The first is a mass-equivalent conversion h/(m_u*c), the second is hc/e; energy and mass units are not interchangeable without c^2.

limitations: The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.

limitations: Neutral carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 u; C-12(6+) instead has mass 12 u minus six electron masses plus the six positive ionization energies divided by c^2. The sixfold charge factor in m_p=R*m_C/6 cannot be omitted.

limitations: Fink/Myers uses a separate FSU 8.5 T, 4.2 K trap with two simultaneously stored ions, alternated between the center and a 2 mm cyclotron orbit. Storage is simultaneous; the reported frequency readout is sequential.

Of 83 runs on 27 H2+ ions, the final analysis uses 33 runs on seven ions. The eight-Gaussian vibrational histogram is not the final mass fit. The supplement needed to audit selection and maximum-likelihood details was not obtained.

Vibrational v=0 does not imply rotational N=0. Long-lived rotational excitation is modeled, not directly measured. A 300 K parent-gas distribution and cascade calculation are assumptions, with uncertain desorption populations.
The adopted rotational correction is 15.8(16.4) ppt. The trend -5.1(12.4) ppt is not a detection of heating. Table III total correction is 65.2(19.0) ppt; the 19.0 includes statistical uncertainty.

The published final ratio uncertainty components are (7) statistical, (7) instrumental, (16) rotational and (19) total. The raw statistical entry is 6.3 ppt; the original weighting is not independently reproduced.

limitations: Three H2+ ions give eleven plateaus (2, 6 and 3). The final three conditional branch means use five ratios with unique level assignments within each branch, not eleven independently assigned ground-state measurements.

Assignments use theoretical level spacings, polarizability and E2 selection rules. The discarded high branch requires initial N>=7 and is rejected using a population prior, not direct state readout. Moss 1993, Korobov 2018 and the population/polarizability inputs remain unreviewed upstream.

The three uncorrected R00(5 ms) values are 0.9992316599712(21), 0.9992316599589(29) and 0.9992316599550(27). Relative branch probabilities are estimated between 1:0.012:0.058 and 1:0.13:0.27; the missing supplement prevents replay of those probabilities.

The published mass ratio assumes the most probable assignment. The other two branches lower it by 2.7 or 3.6 quoted standard uncertainties. These discrete alternatives are not included in the stated conditional Gaussian uncertainty and are not uniquely excluded.
H2+ ground-state ionization energy is 131058.1219937(6) cm^-1 in Korobov 2017 Table V. It is distinct from the HD+ entry and from the older binding calculations cited in Fink 2020.

The NRQED calculation uses CODATA 2014 constants and spin-averaged energies. The quoted uncertainty is theoretical; the separate Rydberg and mass-ratio uncertainties are excluded. Wavefunctions, higher-order approximations and code are not replayed.
Use m_H2=2*m_p+m_e-E_ion(H2+)/c^2. Since both ions carry one positive charge, R=nu(H2+)/nu(D+)=m_d/m_H2. A reciprocal ratio or positive binding addition is a different equation.

claims.statement: In the ideal corrected beam model, R_p=epsilon_p*N_n/tau and R_monitor=epsilon_0*v_0*N_n/L, so tau=L*epsilon_p*R_monitor/(epsilon_0*v_0*R_p). R_p counts detected proton-producing decays, and epsilon_0 is the monitor efficiency at the reference speed v_0.

citations.locator: Published PDF pages 1-5, Sections I-II and Equations 3-8: publication identity, decay counting, neutron population, inverse-velocity monitor and trap-length slope
citations.note: Only the stated acquisition, monitor calibration or conditional inference is supported by this reviewed passage.

limitations: The measured beam observable is a proton-producing decay rate relative to the monitored neutron population in the trapping region. Identifying its inverse with the total free-neutron lifetime requires the stated decay-channel and detection assumptions. Storage disappearance and proton counting are distinct observables; no branching fraction or explanation of their difference is inferred here.

Cancellation of the neutron velocity distribution assumes a thin monitor with inverse-velocity response and unchanged beam between the trap and monitor. Finite absorption, spatial profiles, scattering and beam transport still require the original corrections.

The effective trap length is L=n*l+L_end. A fit of the proton-to-monitor count-rate ratio versus electrode number removes a constant end contribution only under the common-end-region assumption; the paper separately corrects nonlinearity from field, geometry and beam divergence. Proton trapping for milliseconds is not neutron storage for a lifetime.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.

limitations: The ideal transfer identity uses R_Pu=r_Pu,stack/Omega_stack, Omega_AG=r_Pu,AG/R_Pu and R_n=r_gamma,thick*r_alpha,thin/(r_gamma,thin*Omega_AG). The beam analysis uses timed beam-on minus beam-off rates, the geometric mean of top and bottom gamma-detector rates, and thin-target/thick-target/thin-target cycles to suppress first-order gamma-efficiency drift. Gamma backgrounds, thresholds, pulse pileup, dead time and silicon-capture contributions remain explicit corrections; a count-rate ratio is not a raw absolute neutron count.

Within-campaign gamma-detector drift controls are distinct from the long-term 6Li-deposit and aperture stability assumptions needed to transfer a later calibration to the 2000-2001 lifetime acquisition. The thesis Chapter 8 treated that transfer as unresolved; the separately reviewed 2013 update adopts its stated temporal-stability model. No deposit-loss posterior or historical transfer is independently reproduced here.

Cancellation of nuclear normalization inputs in the ideal rate identity does not eliminate nuclear data from every correction. The detailed article uses neutron scattering/absorption inputs, radiative-capture cross sections, material attenuation and modeled neutron/gamma transport. Its remaining upstream nuclear data, image records and simulation implementations are not independently reproduced.

The wavelength is inferred from silicon Bragg measurements on the same beam, including a lambda/2 component correction. Unexplained angle excursions are retained and the wavelength uncertainty uses a conservative observed spread, rather than only the uncertainty of the weighted centroid. The wavelength fit and transport simulations are not replayed.

The 27 reported calibration points span three collimations and two gamma detectors with common and configuration-specific corrections. The article describes Gaussian variation of correction inputs followed by weighted constant fits. These points, detector channels and publications do not supply independent replications of the calibration standard; full correction covariance, exact grouping and analysis code are not recovered from printed tables.

Equation 28 in the 2018 article omits the factor 1/2 required to invert Equation 12, which counts both alpha and triton products. Equation 26 defines phi_abs as an absorbed fraction near 0.01016, but the later text labels the transmission correction 0.989846 as phi_abs. These printed formula/notation conflicts are retained; no claim is made that the numerical implementation followed them.

Source-specific normalization, metrology, corrections and aggregation must be reconciled before substitution. No new lifetime is calculated from the 2018 value and these reports are not averaged.

GE(0)=1 and GM(0)=mu_p specify reference normalization; the measured cross section does not determine signs by itself.

limitations: The 2014 author report describes the August 2006, November 2006 and May 2007 MAMI acquisition previously reported in 2010. The 2010 and 2014 publications, spline fits and Rosenbluth separation are dependent uses of this acquisition, not independent replications.

The released ratios are a fitted-normalization data product, with spline-derived error scaling; they are not a temporally prior independent input to that same fit. The cross-section ratios already incorporate acceptance and radiation modeling, Feshbach Coulomb correction and spline-fit normalization. They are not raw counts or independently measured absolute Born cross sections. Standard-dipole normalization is a model input.

The 31 normalization parameters enter shared products. Equation 48 multiplies data and error by their product; ancillary Section 4 uses the reciprocal nuisance-parameter convention on the model. Their numerical parameter values are not interchangeable. Column 6 contains already-scaled point-to-point errors, not counting errors to scale a second time. limitations: The channel is an isolated ground-state bare deuteron with no supplied energy and asymptotically free p+p+e-+electron-antineutrino final particles. Its net charge is +1 on both sides. Neutral atoms, electronic bound final states, molecular ions and externally driven breakup are different state specifications.

Q0 neglects the antineutrino rest mass; any nonnegative final neutrino mass raises the required rest energy. Positive-energy on-shell final particles and four-momentum conservation make Q0<0 an exclusion for this channel. Q0>=0 alone would not establish a nonzero matrix element or rate.

The calculation uses the one Rau joint adjusted pair mp=1.007276466580(17)u and md=2.013553212537(16)u with correlation +0.26. These reuse the published mass measurements and molecular/reference inputs; the local adjustment, direct deuteron and earlier proton values are not substituted or pooled as independent replicas.

The adopted CODATA 2018 inputs are me=0.000548579909065(16)u and u*c^2=931494102.42(28)eV. They are external adjustment values, not new electron-mass or energy-conversion measurements; this calculation does not update them to a later adjustment.

The admitted neutron mass was inferred as mn=md-mp+Bd/c^2 using the same adjusted masses and capture binding. Substitution into (mn-mp-me)c^2-Bd cancels Bd identically. Capture-derived mn and Bd are not independent confirmation of the reduced Q and cannot be assigned independent errors in that expression.

Separately inserting printed mn=1.00866491604u and Bd/c^2=0.00238817008u gives a Q larger by 0.0027944823...eV than the reduced expression. The identity gives mn=1.008664916037u, compatible with the printed neutron rounding; the difference is not a source-analysis error or a second acquisition. The display-rounding box is not a confidence interval.

The published +0.26 mass-pair correlation enters var(md-2mp)=var(md)+4var(mp)-4cov(md,mp), giving about 0.0313eV standard uncertainty for this contribution alone. Electron/reference cross-covariances and the full adjustment are not reconstructed; no complete Q uncertainty, discovery significance or calibrated coverage is supplied.

Bare nuclear masses cannot be replaced by neutral hydrogen-isotope masses. For positive electronic binding energies IH and ID, Q0=[M(D)-2M(H)]c^2+ID-2IH. This identity retains the declared bare-particle channel; it does not import a neutral-atom decay or its final electronic states.

This is a new bounded calculation from published inputs, not a beta-decay measurement reported by Rau. It establishes neither all-channel deuteron permanence, a nuclear or individual bound-neutron lifetime, nor stability of arbitrary nuclei. No weak amplitude, phase-space rate, raw mass fit, instrument calibration or complete covariance is reproduced.

The cascade hypothesis is K-+p -> Omega-+K++K0, followed by Omega- -> Xi0+pi-, Xi0 -> Lambda0+pi0, Lambda0 -> p+pi- and pi0 -> gamma+gamma with photon conversions. The Lambda fit, photon pairing, transverse balance and missing-mass checks share this event; they are not independent replications.

Strangeness -3 is inferred using the reconstructed Xi0 channel, the weak-decay Delta S=1 assumption and competing-channel reasoning. Charge and mass support a conditional Omega identification; the one-event evidence does not measure J^P=3/2+ or establish the full decuplet dynamics.
The reported 0.7e-10 s is the reconstructed proper decay time of this event, not an ensemble mean lifetime or a lifetime fit. Neither a branching fraction nor all-channel stability follows.

The report gives 1686 +/- 12 MeV/c^2 while explicitly deferring a detailed mass discussion until more events and better-understood systematic errors. No new confidence-level meaning, independent significance, modern mass combination or numerical reconstruction of that uncertainty is assigned.

claims.statement: In the stated solar-neutrino weak-response model, nu_e+d->p+p+e-minus is the charged-current channel, nu_x+d->p+n+nu_x is the neutral-current channel and nu_x+e-minus->nu_x+e-minus is elastic scattering. limitations: The 4353 fully contained events include multiple-ring samples listed in Table I; the oscillation analysis uses only single-ring FC events. The 301 partially contained events have no single-ring requirement and are assigned mu-like on the simulated 98% muon-neutrino charged-current composition. These are reconstructed and selected candidates, not original photomultiplier records or pure incoming-flavor counts. Detailed selection/reconstruction references [6,7] are not independently replayed.

E_vis is the energy of an electron producing the same Cherenkov light, not the incoming neutrino energy; the sub-GeV/multi-GeV boundary is 1330 MeV in that visible variable. Charged-lepton direction and momentum are imperfect proxies for neutrino direction/energy. The mean neutrino-lepton angle quoted by the source changes from 55 degrees at 400 MeV/c to 20 degrees at 1.5 GeV/c; low-momentum angular structure is smeared.

Selected counts, double ratios, asymmetries, zenith distributions, reconstructed L/E and the fitted interpretation reuse this 535-day acquisition. The two analysis groups and the R-versus-shape cross-checks are not independent exposures. Figure 2 also displays earlier Kamiokande limits, and the paper mentions preliminary upward-muon studies; neither is admitted as a separate dataset here. No latest-result or complete later-Super-Kamiokande review is claimed.

limitations: The reported fit uses 70 particle-type, momentum and zenith bins, weighted Monte Carlo statistics and nuisance penalties from Equations 2-4 and Table II. Overall normalization alpha floats freely despite an estimated 25% prior uncertainty; it is not included as a 25% Gaussian constraint. The v2 multi-GeV FC mu-like weight contains (1-rho*N_PC/(2*N_mu)), whereas PC has (1+rho/2). Neither weights, response, minimization, contour coverage nor significance are locally reconstructed.

The physical best fit has sin^2(2 theta)=1 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2; the unconstrained minimum at sin^2(2 theta)=1.05 lies outside the physical region. Reported confidence contours are referenced to the physical minimum with the authors' bounded-region prescription, not generic two-parameter thresholds supplied locally. This is a historical effective two-flavor mass-squared difference, not an absolute mass, a modern three-flavor global fit or a mass-generation mechanism.

limitations: The reported fit uses 70 particle-type, momentum and zenith bins, weighted Monte Carlo statistics and nuisance penalties from Equations 2-4 and Table II. Overall normalization alpha floats freely despite an estimated 25% prior uncertainty; it is not included as a 25% Gaussian constraint. The v2 multi-GeV FC mu-like weight contains (1-rho*N_PC/(2*N_mu)), whereas PC has (1+rho/2). Neither weights, response, minimization, contour coverage nor significance are locally reconstructed.

The physical best fit has sin^2(2 theta)=1 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2; the unconstrained minimum at sin^2(2 theta)=1.05 lies outside the physical region. Reported confidence contours are referenced to the physical minimum with the authors' bounded-region prescription, not generic two-parameter thresholds supplied locally. This is a historical effective two-flavor mass-squared difference, not an absolute mass, a modern three-flavor global fit or a mass-generation mechanism.

The nu_mu-to-nu_tau simulation neglects tau appearance and decay because of the small expected yield. The source explicitly says this sample cannot distinguish nu_mu-to-nu_tau from disappearance into a non-interacting sterile species; it does not directly observe tau appearance. Its separate nu_mu-to-nu_e comparison includes Earth matter effects and is disfavored within the tested model, not an exclusion of every alternative theory.

The atmospheric flux, neutrino-nucleus interactions, particle identification and detector response condition the predicted event samples. Table I uses the flux calculation cited as reference [2]; alternative flux calculations and control samples constrain source-specific uncertainties. The quoted flavor purities and roughly 20% variation of absolute flux predictions are model-dependent inputs, not directly measured neutrino populations. No flux, interaction generator, control data, raw response or covariance is reconstructed.

Selected counts, double ratios, asymmetries, zenith distributions, reconstructed L/E and the fitted interpretation reuse this 535-day acquisition. The two analysis groups and the R-versus-shape cross-checks are not independent exposures. Figure 2 also displays earlier Kamiokande limits, and the paper mentions preliminary upward-muon studies; neither is admitted as a separate dataset here. No latest-result or complete later-Super-Kamiokande review is claimed.

Figure 4 uses only FC events with momentum above 400 MeV/c and a reconstructed L/E estimate from lepton kinematics and modeled production heights. PC events have no assigned momentum in Figure 1. The L/E display is a same-acquisition cross-check, not an independently reconstructed neutrino path, a resolved oscillation dip or a new exposure.

claims.statement: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.
claims.scope: Formal coherent propagation in a prescribed ordinary medium and its stated two-flavor approximation; no empirical mass-generation or solar-fit claim.

citations.locator: 2025 review pages 10-12, Section 14.5 and Equations 14.49-14.58: coherent forward potentials, neutral matter, propagation basis and particle-sign conventions
citations.note: Supports the selected formal convention and its stated model limits; no experimental inference is admitted by this definition.

limitations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism, universal carrier minima or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.

claims.statement: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. The eigenvalue gap is Delta_m/(2E), with cos(2 theta_m)=(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)/Delta_m and sin(2 theta_m)=Delta*sin(2 theta)/Delta_m. Nonzero mixing is maximal at A=Delta*cos(2 theta). An instantaneous eigenbasis has the additional connection -i*R-dagger*dR/dx; adiabatic following is an approximation that neglects its inter-state coupling relative to the gap.

limitations: The two-flavor formula is a separately declared closed nu_e/nu_x approximation, with nu_x an active mu/tau combination, Delta=m2^2-m1^2>0, 0<theta<pi/2, E>0 and a nonzero instantaneous gap. It is not an exact reduction of every three-flavor preparation. The sine and cosine specify the angle branch; tan(2 theta_m) alone is insufficient.

A=Delta*cos(2 theta) gives maximal instantaneous mixing only when the off-diagonal mixing and gap are nonzero. Resonance by itself does not establish adiabatic following, complete flavor conversion, equal observed event rates or an experimentally selected mechanism. Antineutrino propagation uses the opposite matter potential.

If f=R(x)*a in an instantaneous eigenbasis, i*da/dx=[diag(lambda_i)-i*R-dagger*dR/dx]*a. Neglecting the off-diagonal derivative coupling requires it to be small compared with the relevant eigenvalue gap along the path, with nondegenerate and sufficiently smooth evolution. Abrupt changes or a small gap can invalidate that approximation. No solar survival probability or fitted density profile is supplied.

limitations: Use the existing closed nu_e/nu_x approximation with Delta=m2^2-m1^2>0 and 0<theta<pi/4; nu_x is the stated active mu/tau combination. Adiabaticity requires the off-diagonal basis-derivative coupling |d theta_m/dx| to be small compared with the instantaneous eigenvalue gap along the actual path, together with smooth evolution to the vacuum endpoint. The exponential profile by itself does not establish that condition. No numerical check over a solar path is claimed.

The interference terms must be sufficiently smeared by the actual source, baseline and detector resolution/weights. A long baseline alone is not a replacement for this averaging condition, and averaged probabilities do not mean that the local forward-scattering Hamiltonian is incoherent. Page 14 prints Delta m^2/E >> L_Sun-Earth; this dimensionally inconsistent statement is not used. The relevant phase is dimensionless Delta m^2 L/(4E), with averaging as in Equations 14.40-14.42.

At fixed mixing angle the low-density limit A_p/Delta -> 0 gives P_ee -> 1-sin^2(2 theta)/2, while A_p/Delta -> infinity gives P_ee -> sin^2(theta) under the same adiabatic and phase-averaging conditions. Merely crossing resonance, A_p>Delta cos(2 theta), does not make the high-density limit exact and does not guarantee adiabaticity.

The production density includes the spatial measure as written, is source-component dependent and may depend on energy; it is not n_e(R), a delta function at the solar center or a fitted distribution in this graph. The source spectrum, production distribution, density normalization and detector weights are all external inputs. No actual production/energy integral, event spectrum, covariance or fit is evaluated.

The endpoint is the exposed Earth surface before terrestrial matter propagation. Earth regeneration, nonadiabatic jump probabilities, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require additional models. For elastic scattering or neutral-current channels, the corresponding flavor-dependent response must be folded explicitly; a single electron-flavor charged-current weight is not a universal event-rate formula.

The model is not inferred by subtracting SNO fluxes or by pooling solar, reactor and accelerator acquisitions. It does not establish an absolute mass, mass-generation mechanism, flavor-object identity, necessary formation order, universal parent weight or carrier minimum.

limitations: Use the closed unitary active two- or three-state convention already declared. Oscillatory flavor probabilities require both mixing of contributing components and nonzero relative mass-squared differences, together with the stated production/detection and propagation coherence conditions. A degenerate pair, unmixed channel or suppressed interference need not show an oscillatory signal.

A single vacuum mass eigenstate acquires only a phase in its internal state; its flavor-readout probabilities |U_alpha,i|^2 do not oscillate. An incoherent density matrix diagonal in the vacuum mass basis also has constant vacuum flavor probabilities. These are not statements that vacuum mass states remain instantaneous eigenstates in arbitrary varying matter, or that packet position is stationary.

Leptonic charged-current flavor labels specify preparation/readout; mass differences and mixing specify model inputs. They do not establish necessary physical parents, an arising chronology, weights 0.3/0.7, N_min=N_crit=1, a SOMA phase/type or the claim that flavor identity can never be dynamically autonomous. No causal maintenance or downward constraint is inferred from these definition dependencies.

Within this oscillation model, mass-squared differences constrain differences only. They do not determine the absolute mass scale, require every individual mass to be nonzero, select Dirac versus Majorana character or supply a unique mass-generation extension. Mass origin remains a separate scope.

Continuous weak scattering or repeated projective collapse is not the coherent phase mechanism. A specified source, medium and detector determine which probability or weighted response is appropriate; transport and cosmological claims need additional inputs.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

claims.statement: The reported calculation uses a 24^3 x 48 lattice, a=0.145 fm, three degenerate clover flavors and a tree-level-improved Luscher-Weisz gauge action at pion mass approximately 800 MeV. The source compares GEVP, symmetric/block Lanczos and asymmetric-correlator analyses of these related correlators.

limitations: The 2026 calculation is not a new independent repeat of all three 2013 volumes. Shared gauge fields, action and scale coexist with changed propagator sampling, operators and analysis. Configurations and propagators are not independent experimental events.

Treating finite-time energy estimators as eigenvalues requires the stated N-state-saturation assumption. Symmetric variational upper bounds do not exclude missed lower levels. Residual bounds require a Hermitian transfer matrix and delimit a window containing some eigenvalue, not necessarily the ground state; for this improved action the source restricts Hermiticity to its low-energy sector, E much less than 1/a.

Tighter gap bounds require the stated no-missing-states threshold and negligible thermal effects. Estimates based on noninteracting NN level counts below NDelta or DeltaDelta thresholds can fail if extra low states are present. Source errors and bound widths are distinct; one-sided upper bounds cannot supply two-sided phase errors.

The selected phase comparison truncates to the lowest S wave, neglects lattice artifacts and does not determine a complete coupled-channel amplitude. Raw correlators, residual/gap calculations, operator completeness, continuum/infinite-volume extrapolations and physical-mass nuclear binding are not reproduced here.

claims.statement: The paired 2026 preprints leave the nature of the lowest I=1 and I=0 two-nucleon states at these heavy-mass action parameters unresolved without additional spectral assumptions. This does not exclude a missed bound state or validate the earlier binding assignment as consensus.
