limitations: This record synthesizes the reported primary numerical analysis and its methodological conclusion. It is neither a new measured energy nor an independent simulation; the two preprints describe the same work and are not pooled confirmations.

A negative finite-volume energy shift relative to two nucleons is not by itself an infinite-volume bound-state determination. Residual/gap intervals can contain an eigenvalue without establishing its ground-state index or excluding additional levels outside the interval. The source tables distinguish statistical confidence from assumption-dependent spectral windows.

The asymmetric-correlator diagnostics show changing left/right state overlaps over accessible Euclidean times. They question the eigenstate interpretation of apparently stable estimators without proving that every such energy estimate is wrong or that a bound state cannot exist.

The reported synthetic small-gap examples use chosen spectra, overlaps and a noise model related to the lattice data. Their statistically similar bound/scattering outputs illustrate an inverse-problem ambiguity; they are not additional QCD measurements or a unique reconstruction of the true spectrum.

Neither the single-volume 2026 analysis nor the conditional 2013 interpretation establishes continuum physical-mass nuclear binding, all nuclei, atomic binding, a real-time formation rate or permanent matter stability.

limitations: A renormalized quark mass needs a prescription and scale. The new flavor-symmetric calculation specifies one action-dependent bare mass; it does not determine an MSbar mass or its response derivative. Flavor SU(3), with degenerate up, down and strange masses, is distinct from the SU(3) color gauge symmetry of QCD.

Controlled quark-mass sensitivity requires a defined input variation or derivative and a declaration of what is held fixed, including the gauge coupling or QCD scale, cutoff, strange/sea masses and unit calibration. A comparison with physical nuclear data alone is not such a controlled calculation. An input hadron mass used to set the scale cannot simultaneously count as an independent prediction.

Hadron masses, nuclear binding differences, bulk density, compressibility and astrophysical matter are different observables. No reviewed many-body equation of state, composition, thermodynamic state, pressure response or astrophysical inference is supplied here. Direct quark-to-density/compressibility edges and a demonstrated uninterrupted chain to macroscopic materials are excluded, without asserting that the underlying physical influence is zero.

Generic nuclear-model, observation and astrophysical evidence placeholders identify no preparation or discriminator and supply no additional evidence. The measurements do not establish exactly zero photon mass or charge, distinguishable persistent identity, a static Coulomb photon flux, atomic binding, an oriented vacuum or universal photon-driven biological organization. These boundaries remain those of the formal scope definition.

claims.statement: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.
claims.scope: A declared PMNS convention and phase-counting boundary; not measured angle values, CP violation or a determination of neutrino mass character.

limitations: The supplied 3-by-3 unitary model is distinct from a general 3-by-n charged-current matrix or an effective light-sector submatrix after heavy states are removed. The latter need not be exactly unitary; this definition does not establish that extra states are absent.

The phase count assumes generic nondegenerate nonzero masses. Degenerate masses, a massless state or vanishing mixing angles can remove phases or their observable effects. A nontrivial mixing matrix need not violate CP, and a complex entry alone is not a rephasing-invariant measurement.

For the same ordinary vacuum channel, U_prime(alpha,i)=exp(i r_alpha) U(alpha,i) exp(i c_i) gives A_prime(alpha,beta)=exp(i(r_beta-r_alpha)) A(alpha,beta), so its probability is unchanged. This column-phase invariance of the oscillation amplitude does not permit arbitrary rephasing of a Majorana field at fixed real mass in the full Lagrangian.

Majorana column-phase cancellation concerns ordinary lepton-number-conserving oscillations. It does not make those phases unphysical in all processes or identify neutrinos as Dirac or Majorana. The chosen angles, phases and conventions supply no fitted parameter values or current ordering preference.

claims.statement: With the usual fermion content, one Higgs doublet and no right-handed neutrino singlets, the minimal renormalizable Standard Model has no neutrino Dirac Yukawa term and leaves neutrinos massless. Formal extensions can add singlet neutrinos and Dirac masses, with total lepton number imposed to exclude Majorana terms, or allow lepton-number-violating Majorana masses. A dimension-five operator built from the lepton and Higgs doublets can instead generate a Majorana mass after electroweak symmetry breaking. These are alternative model constructions; flavor-oscillation evidence alone does not select one.
claims.scope: Formal boundary between the minimal massless theory and possible massive-neutrino extensions; no measured ultraviolet mechanism.

limitations: The massless statement uses the minimal renormalizable field content and its accidental symmetries. It is not a prohibition on all gauge-invariant Standard Model effective operators: the stated dimension-five extension changes that assumption.

Dirac and Majorana alternatives require different field or symmetry assumptions. A see-saw construction additionally needs a hierarchy and matching assumptions; no such hierarchy, heavy state, Yukawa coefficient or new-physics scale is inferred here.

Nonzero oscillation mass-squared differences do not determine all absolute masses, prove that all three masses are positive, identify a Dirac/Majorana assignment, or establish the charged-fermion mass route for neutrinos. Direct kinematic, cosmological and lepton-number-violating searches retain separate inference contexts.

claims.statement: In the leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model with hbar=c=1, hold U, L and E fixed. Replacing every m_i^2 by m_i^2+kappa multiplies A_alpha-to-beta by exp[-i kappa L/(2E)], leaving P=|A|^2 unchanged. This holds for shifts preserving m_i^2+kappa>=0 and (m_i^2+kappa)/E^2<<1. For three nonnegative squared masses, Delta21=m_2^2-m_1^2 and Delta31=m_3^2-m_1^2 both nonzero and unequal imply three pairwise distinct values; at most one can be zero, so at least two masses are nonzero.
claims.scope: Formal identifiability of squared-mass differences in a supplied leading three-state vacuum oscillation model.

limitations: This is a conditional algebraic consequence of the declared leading vacuum phase, not a new measurement, global fit or independent replication of mass splittings. Fixed preparation, energy and detector response are assumed; endpoint kinematics, time of flight, coherence conditions and higher-order dispersion are not covered by this invariance.

An admissible common shift changes the absolute mass scale without changing these probabilities. No unique absolute masses, measured upper bound, mass ordering, Dirac versus Majorana character or mass-generation mechanism follows from this statement. Keeping the ultrarelativistic approximation valid is not an experimentally inferred upper bound.

Two nonzero differences alone are insufficient: (m_1^2,m_2^2,m_3^2)=(q,0,0), q>0, gives Delta21=Delta31=-q and only one nonzero mass. The unequal-differences condition excludes this degeneracy. Conversely (0,a,b), with a,b>0 and a!=b, meets the condition while one mass is zero; all three need not be nonzero.

The three-state and nonnegative-mass assumptions are explicit. Separate historical effective two-flavor fits are not automatically a joint closed three-state likelihood; their best-fit numbers are not identified here with exact three-state splittings or pooled into new constraints.

limitations: A charged-current flavor label is tied to the accompanying charged-lepton preparation/readout; it is not an individual propagation mass, a classical mixture measured simultaneously in two bases or a guarantee that every neutrino state exhibits flavor oscillation. Closed three-active unitarity is a supplied model restriction, not an exclusion of every additional state or nonunitary effective submatrix.

The minimal renormalizable Standard Model with its stated field content has no neutrino mass term. Charged-fermion Higgs/Yukawa relations do not automatically supply neutrino masses. Alternative massive-neutrino field/operator assignments are formal inputs, not a measured Dirac/Majorana choice, a unique origin or a prediction of mixing parameters.

At fixed mixing, baseline and energy in the declared leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum phase, an admissible common mass-squared shift leaves oscillation probabilities unchanged. Two unequal nonzero mass-squared differences from a shared reference imply three distinct eigenvalues and at least two positive masses, not three positive masses. Equal nonzero differences are not sufficient for that conclusion. Selected effective two-flavor fits are not automatically exact three-state eigenpair measurements.

Oscillation evidence here does not determine an absolute mass scale, the mass ordering beyond its selected conditional models, Dirac/Majorana character, Majorana phases, sterile content or the origin of the mixing/Yukawa parameters. No beta-endpoint, neutrinoless-double-beta, cosmological mass-sum or modern global-fit bounds are imported.

Propagation, coherence and applications retain the separate scope of card 1.17. The matter Hamiltonian uses vacuum masses/mixing as inputs; its medium potential does not generate those vacuum masses. Source composition, collisions, self-refraction, cosmic expansion and detector response require their own quantitative transport inputs. This admission supplies no astrophysical transport or cosmological prediction.

The original necessary lepton parent is retained only as a descriptive flavor-readout/model dependency. Weight 1, Nmin=Ncrit=1, arising/maintenance and direction/interaction codes do not establish a measured formation threshold, universal causal necessity or temporal emergence sequence. SOMA phase 1, property/type-role 3 and the established label are not scientific evidence.

The original refusal to specify a deeper mass-generation mechanism is preserved. Finite evidence for mass-induced mixing under declared assumptions does not require selecting a speculative mechanism; it also does not validate every flavor-transformation explanation or a universal sector-wide construction.

limitations: KamLAND contributes its reactor-only rate-and-shape two-flavor fit; its shape-only and CPT-assuming solar-combined analyses are not new reactor acquisitions. The 1998 Super-Kamiokande atmospheric fit is a historical effective two-flavor result conditioned on flux, response and nuisance assumptions; it did not directly distinguish tau from sterile disappearance. Their reported characteristic splitting scales are not relabeled as exact modern three-state eigenpairs or combined into a new likelihood.

The SNO-only direct joint electron/non-electron active-flux inference supports solar flavor transformation under its B8-shape and response assumptions. It is not NC-minus-CC subtraction of independent fluxes, a separate muon/tau identification, an oscillation-phase or mass-splitting measurement, or proof of a unique matter-enhanced mechanism. Its SK-added solar constraint is not the distinct 1998 atmospheric exposure.

OPERA appearance significance, signal strength and its full-mixing mass-squared interval reuse the same 2008-2012 acquisition, channel counts and response. The compatibility result is not independent appearance replication or a third distinct oscillation frequency. Its adopted nominal splitting and full-mixing inputs are not additional fitted observations; the reported intervals and significance retain their original confidence construction.

These are four named inference contexts and five outcomes, not five independent experiments or a global three-flavor fit. Event selections, intermediate summaries, alternative analysis implementations and fitted outputs within a campaign share data. No likelihood, nuisance covariance, combined parameter range, mass ordering or confidence coverage is newly reconstructed.

Within a supplied common three-state mass-induced interpretation, distinct nonzero splitting scales motivate the formal identifiability consequence of at least two nonzero masses. This comparison does not independently establish all assumptions of that embedding or measure all three masses, an absolute scale, Dirac/Majorana nature, Majorana phases, sterile content or a unique mechanism. The formal common-shift invariance is not a new experimental bound.

Generic solar, atmospheric, reactor and accelerator evidence placeholders are restricted to these actual admitted sources and analysis stages. Astrophysical/cosmological constraints, beta endpoints, neutrinoless double beta decay and universal parent/formation/maintenance claims remain excluded from this finite evidence comparison.

claims.statement: Adopt the local gauge algebra su(3)c plus su(2)L plus u(1)Y, conventionally written SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y, with Q=T3+Y. For each of three generations, the pre-Higgs-background chiral assignments are Q_L=(u_L,dprime_L)~(3,2,1/6), u_R~(3,1,2/3), d_R~(3,1,-1/3), L_L=(nu_L,l_L)~(1,2,-1/2) and l_R~(1,1,-1). The single complex Higgs scalar is phi~(1,2,1/2). Each tuple gives the color representation, weak representation and declared hypercharge: 3 means the color fundamental, 2 the weak doublet and 1 a singlet. The gauge potentials are G_mu^a (a=1,...,8), W_mu^i (i=1,2,3) and B_mu, with couplings gs, g and gprime. This is a chosen interacting field specification; the scalar is a boson without being a gauge vector mediator.

limitations: The envelope must be smooth and sufficiently narrow in momentum for expansion about k0 over the stated propagation interval. Higher dispersion derivatives can spread or reshape it; this velocity approximation does not assert exact rigid translation. A changing local amplitude or escape from a finite region is not by itself intrinsic decay.

A sharp momentum eigenstate is delta-normalized and not a bounded localized object. Use suitably smeared, normalized finite-energy states. The positive-frequency envelope is a mode-superposition description, not a universal relativistic position probability density or proof of persistent localization.

Rotation covariance changes the velocity vector components; it does not make rotation-related momentum labels or states identical. Equal speed compares fixed |k|, mass and model with the preparation rotated consistently. A chosen packet momentum can select a propagation direction without introducing an intrinsic vacuum axis; k=0 has no momentum direction.

This is a closed free model with a time-independent Hamiltonian, without interaction-induced transitions, dissipation or an imposed directional environment. Conservation of its free number sector and a mode phase do not establish the persistence of all interacting excitations, every quantum state or an open subsystem. Physical boundaries or anisotropic regulators require a separate symmetry analysis.

Group velocity is the local narrow-envelope velocity derived here. It is not an integrated particle or energy flux, a signal-front speed, detector retention, a net directed current or propulsion. No transport measurement, decay width, localization length, damping rate, numerical replay or universal stability threshold is admitted.

limitations: A dispersion relation specifies frequency versus momentum; it is not a damping law, attenuation length, localization length or intrinsic decay width. Only within the declared exponential-survival approximation does the PDG convention give tau_proper=1/Gamma and P(t_lab)=exp(-Gamma*t_lab/gamma) in hbar=c=1, with Gamma an energy width and gamma the fixed Lorentz factor. This is a formal decay convention, not an exact survival law at every time, a new complex-pole calculation or a measured lifetime. Detector linewidth, instrumental broadening, scattering and path attenuation cannot automatically become intrinsic decay width.

A unit-modulus free-mode phase and conservation of the full state norm do not alone establish persistence of a selected unstable component or spatially localized packet. Unitary evolution can transfer amplitude out of a selected subspace. The supplied free model preserves its Fock number sector, but this does not freeze the packet shape or generalize to interacting or open subsystems.

Comparing different axes at fixed momentum magnitude is distinct from comparing opposite directions in one specified apparatus. Spatial anisotropy does not by itself establish opposite-direction nonreciprocity, a preferred drift or net transport. A directional comparison must hold the model, frame, preparation and apparatus controls appropriately fixed; no selected anisotropic environment or response protocol is supplied here.

claims.statement: In the selected homogeneous hot-expanding model, weak neutron/proton interconversion, expansion and thermodynamics set a reaction history for free nucleons and light nuclei. Abundances may be expressed per baryon as Y_i=n_i/n_b; a nuclear species balance has dilution dn_i/dt+3*H*n_i and a sum of reaction production and destruction terms. The deuterium photodissociation bottleneck delays effective light-nucleus assembly; nuclear reactions then produce deuterium, helium-3 and helium-4 and mass-seven species including beryllium-7, which later feeds lithium-7. These model equations require a supplied cosmological background, baryon density, weak rates, neutron lifetime and thermonuclear cross sections.

claims.statement: Adopt the selected equilibrium continuum-solvent ion-atmosphere model in its original electrostatic-cgs units. For electroneutral bulk sum_i(n_i*z_i)=0, the Boltzmann density n_i(r)=n_i*exp[-z_i*e*psi(r)/(kT)] gives, after weak-potential linearization, nabla^2*psi=kappa^2*psi outside the tagged source, with kappa^2=4*pi*e^2*sum_i(n_i*z_i^2)/(D*kT). In the dilute point-ion limiting model the tagged-charge mean potential is psi(r)=q*exp(-kappa*r)/(D*r). The screening length 1/kappa depends on composition, temperature and solvent response; it represents statistical ion-atmosphere structure rather than an ion-formation event.

claims.statement: In the selected hydrostatic bulk thermodynamic framework, equilibrium criteria use allowed variations under explicit constraints: entropy is maximal at fixed total energy, or energy is minimal at fixed entropy. Write A=U-T*S and G=U-T*S+p*V; the relevant potential and stability comparison depend on what is held fixed. For phases in freely exchanging contact without gravity, electrical effects, solid distortion or capillary tension, equilibrium requires equal temperature, pressure and the potential of each freely exchangeable independently variable component. limitations: The Gibbs passage distinguishes adjacent continuous variations from formation of new phases. It does not supply a nucleation barrier, lifetime distribution, kinetic path, transition-state rate or global catalogue of all possible phases.

The hard-disk continuous hexatic-solid transition is not identified with the particular coalescing-fluid critical endpoint described by Gibbs. No universal Landau expansion, renormalization-group universality class or exact exponent is admitted.

claims.statement: For the declared isothermal uniform bulk linear response, the proper piezoelectric stress tensor is e_ijk=(partial D_i/partial strain_jk) at fixed E,T, equivalently -(partial stress_jk/partial E_i) at fixed strain,T. Its SI units are C/m^2. The piezoelectric strain tensor d relates strain to electric field at fixed stress,T or displacement D to stress at fixed E,T, with units m/V, equivalently C/N. Converting between e and d requires elastic compliance and matching tensor/shear conventions; they are not interchangeable numerical coefficients.

claims.statement: For a free nucleus of mass M, the leading nonrelativistic recoil energy is E_R=E_gamma^2/(2*M*c^2), displacing emission below and absorption above the nuclear transition energy. In the selected bound-solid oscillator account, a recoilless nuclear gamma event leaves the internal vibrational occupation state unchanged. Momentum is still transferred to the bound body; its whole-body translational recoil energy is negligibly small on the stated spectral scale. This zero-phonon channel is a fraction of events, not absence of binding vibrations, zero momentum transfer or a rule that every emitted gamma ray is resonant.

claims.statement: Orbital electron capture consumes a bound electron in a specified nuclear transition and emits an electron neutrino; in the selected 140Pr to 140Ce channel it converts a proton to a neutron, preserves mass number A=140 and lowers nuclear charge Z from 59 to 58. Initial bare 140Pr59+, hydrogenlike 140Pr58+ and heliumlike 140Pr57+ carry zero, one and two bound electrons respectively. EC removes one bound electron while lowering Z by one, so the daughter ionic charge remains the same. Changing the initial ionization state does not change which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent nuclear decay does change the element.
claims.scope: Isotope-, channel- and electronic-occupancy definition for the selected storage-ring orbital EC experiment.

The selected ion experiment is not a chemical-bonding, molecular-solvation, pressure or lattice-embedding experiment; a bound-electron count is a preparation label rather than an emergence minimum.

claims.statement: For the source constant-rate fit in one consistent time frame, parent disappearance obeys N_Pr(t)=N_Pr(0)*exp(-lambda_all*t), with lambda_all=lambda_EC+lambda_betaPlus+lambda_loss. Stable EC-daughter growth obeys N_Ce(t)=N_Pr(0)*lambda_EC/(lambda_all-lambda_loss)*[exp(-lambda_loss*t)-exp(-lambda_all*t)]+N_Ce(0)*exp(-lambda_loss*t). Loss includes residual-gas collisions and electron pickup in the cooler; it is not nuclear decay. The source Table I rates are in the ion rest frame, while Figure 2 times are laboratory times: for a constant Lorentz factor gamma, t_lab=gamma*t_rest and lambda_rest=gamma*lambda_lab.

claims.statement: Produce 140Pr by fragmenting 152Sm projectiles at 508 MeV/u on a 1 g/cm^2 Be target, separate bare 59+, H-like 58+ and He-like 57+ charge states with the FRS, and inject them into the ESR under approximately 1e-11 mbar vacuum. Use stochastic and electron cooling near a stored-beam energy of 400 MeV/u, with an overall cooling time about 2 s. Record non-destructive time-resolved Schottky spectra: circulating ions induce pickup signals, Fourier spectra distinguish mass-to-charge peaks, and peak areas track stored populations. The example uses the 31st harmonic and averages each of 195 spectra over 10.5 s. Mechanical slits suppress feeding from other stored ions. Figure 2 time is laboratory time; the source uses gamma=1.43 to report rest-frame rates.
claims.scope: Publication-specific Pr140 charge-state preparation, cooled storage and non-destructive Schottky acquisition.

claims.statement: The source interprets the selected 140Pr nuclear-spin-1 to 140Ce spin-0 Gamow-Teller channel using H-like initial hyperfine F=1/2 or 3/2. In the allowed approximation only F=1/2 couples to the stated final nuclear-spin-0 plus neutrino-spin-1/2 state. With the source-assumed lower F=1/2 population, its statistical factor (2*I_i+1)/(2*F_i+1)=3/2 accounts for the enhanced H-like versus He-like EC rate. Thus electron occupancy alone is insufficient to specify the channel rate; nuclear/electronic angular momentum and state populations enter the interpretation.

claims.statement: For a declared isotope and electronic state, let I be nuclear spin, J total electronic angular momentum and F the coupled total angular momentum. Define K=F(F+1)-I(I+1)-J(J+1). With A expressed in frequency units, the first-order magnetic-dipole contribution relative to the state centroid is E_F/h=A*K/2; allowed higher-rank terms have separate state-specific constants, including the electric-quadrupole B term. In the selected Cs1337d2D3/2 assignment, J=3/2 and F=2,3,4,5 correspond to supplied I=7/2. The first-order electric-quadrupole term is absent within a J=1/2 electronic level; the Cs ground-state clock is not evidence that every hyperfine transition has a nonzero quadrupole contribution.

Nominal directional-hemispherical reflectance, bidirectional reflectance factor and a whole angular distribution are different. One integral or one direction does not determine the other or uniquely identify microscopic roughness, composition, shape or a scene.

A rough or porous target can have subsurface contributions. These data do not uniquely separate surface from volume scattering, reconstruct a complete electromagnetic boundary solution or measure crystallinity as a necessary cause.

claims.statement: In the selected homogeneous isotropic linear medium, use the convention E(z,t)=Re[E0(omega)*exp(i*k(omega)*z-i*omega*t)] with k(omega)=omega*sqrt(epsilon(omega)*mu(omega)) in absolute SI constitutive units. Writing k=k_real+i*k_imag gives amplitude attenuation exp(-k_imag*z) and phase accumulation k_real*z. For the passive forward branch, k_imag>=0; the corresponding fixed-medium intensity attenuation coefficient is alpha_int=2*k_imag in m^-1. Nonlinear real propagation phase across a pulse bandwidth can produce dispersive waveform deformation, whereas a real phase linear in frequency supplies a delay. A wave number proportional to frequency at fixed speed is not by itself dispersive deformation. These phase effects are distinct from imaginary-part attenuation.

limitations: This is a supplied local, homogeneous, isotropic, linear constitutive model with monochromatic components and a declared causal response. It is not a derivation of all material response from isolated molecular dipoles or a model of every anisotropic, nonlinear, time-dependent, scattering or spatially dispersive medium.

The harmonic convention is exp(i*k*z-i*omega*t). With the passive forward branch Im(k)>=0, amplitude decays as exp(-Im(k)*z), while intensity has the factor2 in its exponent. The absolute SI epsilon and mu in k=omega*sqrt(epsilon*mu) are not unqualified relative constants.

The intensity factor2 follows algebraically from the squared field amplitude in this fixed homogeneous setting. No new measured attenuation coefficient, optical-index spectrum, independent mathematical proof or numerical fit is supplied.

Relating attenuation of a measured finite-aperture beam to absorption needs an actual collection/energy model. Redistribution by scattering, boundary reflection and detector acceptance can change collected flux without that signal alone identifying bulk heat deposition.

A deterministic frequency response and dispersive waveform deformation do not by themselves quantify statistical coherence loss, image blur, random-path scattering, a diffraction point-spread function or a measured signal-front/group delay.

limitations: This source studies an expressed, purified His6-tagged E. coli CAP N-terminal fragment comprising residues1-138. It lacks the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of full-length CAP; no DNA binding, transcription, catalytic turnover, cellular adaptation or physiological response is measured in this selected study.

The protein is supplied as a prepared homodimer. Its composition and two cAMP-binding positions are system-specific inputs/assignments, not a universal two-molecule threshold or proof that all allostery requires oligomerization.

The source supplies a ligand-series experiment at30C and fixed assay protocols. It does not measure a universal folding, hydrogen-bond, electrostatic, hydration or feedback ancestry, and it does not operationalize original parent weights or carrier minima.

The supporting information, raw NMR/ITC acquisition, complete concentration calibration, original fitting implementation and covariance are not independently reviewed or reproduced. All admitted quantities retain publication-supported status.

Chemical shifts report local electronic environments and population averages. Small shifts at the remote cAMP pocket constrain a large mean-environment change under this method; they do not prove exact structural identity, an absence of every atom displacement or purely entropy-only causation.

Existing cAMP-bound CAP structure1G6N supplies molecular models, mapping coordinates and distances; it is not a new three-state atomic structure determination. Unread earlier structure data are not cloned as new experiments.

Relaxation-derived spectral densities, exchange rates and order parameters are model-dependent inferences from NMR signals. In the fast-exchange analysis only kex and pA*pB*(deltaomega)^2 are separately accessible; the excited-state population and shift difference are not independently identified.

The nominal ligation-state comparison is controlled within the source experiment, but exact purity of the assigned singly/doubly liganded populations has not been independently measured here. Concentration controls constrain aggregation under tested conditions, not every alternative process.

Nominal cAMP:CAPN dimer ratios1:1 and2:1 enrich the source-assigned ligation states; finite affinities and stoichiometric mixing do not demonstrate mathematically pure occupancy populations. The source complete-saturation phrasing is not promoted to a new measured purity guarantee.

claims.statement: The biphasic CAPN ITC isotherm is fitted with a sequential-site model. Figure7 reports first/second step Kd=0.04 and4micromolar and corresponding rounded deltaG=-10.3 and-7.5kcal/mol. It reports deltaH=-1.8 and-2.9kcal/mol and total -T*deltaS=-8.5 and-4.6kcal/mol. Thus the second step is less favorable overall in the source interpretation despite a more favorable enthalpy; its relative total entropic penalty is about4kcal/mol. This is negative cooperativity, not sensitivity amplification inferred from a positive Hill slope.

limitations: These are engineered E. coli DHFR/cpLys38/barnase substrate constructs in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, not a universal survey of naturally damaged proteins or an intact-cell misfolding-surveillance experiment.

Proteasome attribution follows the source lysate assay. No separately purified proteasome, newly isolated E1/E2/E3 requirement, new receptor-binding measurement, ATPase-step assay, translocation movie, force measurement or proteasome-inhibitor control is supplied by the selected main panels.

SDS-PAGE/autoradiography quantifies remaining full-length plus ubiquitinated forms as defined by each panel; His6 immunoblotting localizes loss of a terminal epitope. Band loss, tail clipping, complete destruction and production/reuse of free amino acids are different outcomes.

The source tests folded and methotrexate-stabilized proteins. The assays do not establish that only misfolded proteins are degraded, that native proteins are excluded, or that the proteasome itself decides whether a client is damaged.

The engineered linear Ub4 tag has four N-to-C fused ubiquitin moieties with G76V substitutions. It is not a newly measured native Lys48-isopeptide-linked polyubiquitin chain or an independently observed covalent ubiquitination reaction.

No universal requirement for ubiquitination is admitted; the paper itself cites ubiquitin-independent cases as background. Recognition, initiation, unfolding and proteolysis remain distinct, with the detailed unfolding/pulling cycle conditional.

No raw autoradiograms, numerical rate fit, binding constant, precise substrate concentration or kinetic uncertainty is reconstructed. Exact engineered tail amino-acid sequences are not printed in the reviewed main Methods, and no universal20-residue minimum is admitted from data-not-shown observations.
Selected degradation panels use 25 C and 0.5 mM ATP with regeneration; Figure 1 two-domain direction assays use 30 C and are not silently treated as the same condition.

C-terminal tail effects differ between cpLys38 and wild-type DHFR under 320 micromolar methotrexate: the former can be degraded whereas the latter can be clipped while the stabilized DHFR remains. A tag or tail does not guarantee complete degradation of every substrate.

Tail disorder is a source assignment supported by the paper separate4 C nonspecific-protease sensitivity assay and a hydrodynamic statement partly data-not-shown. It is not a newly solved structure or an independent measurement of every tail conformation.

claims.statement: At25 C, adding a C-terminal lysine-less tail permits degradation of N-end-rule-tagged cpLys38 even with 320 micromolar methotrexate; inactivating the N-end residue, replacing acceptor Lys15/Lys17 or deleting the N-tag strongly inhibits it. Shortening the Usignal linker slows DHFR degradation, while either tested C-terminal tail restores faster band loss. Linear Ub4-DHFR without a tail is degraded inefficiently; tail addition accelerates loss. This is a finite tag-and-initiation-region requirement under the lysate protocol, not an all-substrate rule.

limitations: Purified, already synthesized clients and purified E. coli GroEL/SR1/GroES are studied in vitro. The selected data do not observe translation, cellular stress adaptation, protein damage surveillance, routing to proteasomes or organismal proteome reliability.

Adding the GroEL/GroES/ATP protocol is a combined intervention. These panels do not by themselves isolate ATP hydrolysis, individual ATPase steps, capture specificity, every component necessity or all possible active folding effects.

Activity recovery, tryptophan fluorescence, light scattering and size-exclusion elution measure different properties. None alone supplies an atomic native structure, a unique folding path or the fraction of every chain in a single native state.
All readouts and fitted rates come from one publication. No raw traces, new fit, covariance, curve digitization, independent replication or analytically-checked status is supplied.

The source interprets these conditions through aggregation prevention. Its broad passive-cage conclusion is retained as conditional, not a proof that all chaperonins are passive or that no client can experience an active conformational effect.

Rubisco activity requires native-dimer formation. SR1 aliquots are chilled to release GroES and allow released monomers to assemble before the enzyme assay; the readout does not show active Rubisco dimers inside the single-client cis chamber.
Figure 1B compares refolding Rubisco plus BSA with native Rubisco plus BSA and BSA alone in solution; it does not directly measure a matched light-scattering reduction inside GroEL/SR1.

Figure 1 C source inference permits reversible intermediate-sized association plus growth of persistent void-volume material. The data do not show that every aggregate dissolves or that all solution aggregation is reversible.

BSA is a controlled solution additive at 7.5 micromolar, not a missing universal chaperone or a universal concentration threshold. Reported rate constants are apparent source fits without newly reconstructed errors.

The DM-MBP client is mature V8G/Y283D maltose-binding protein. Tryptophan fluorescence is an environment-sensitive refolding proxy; no maltose-binding affinity, transport activity or enzymatic client assay is measured here.

The chloride-containing protocol uses 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 6 M guanidine-HCl. The chloride-deficient protocol uses 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 9.5 M urea. Buffer, salt concentration/anion and starting denaturant all change; chloride alone is not isolated.

Concentration dependence and light scattering support intermolecular association under the tested solution protocol. They do not identify a unique oligomer structure or prove that every fluorescence intermediate is an aggregate.

Rate equivalence in the changed solution protocol constrains a need for a faster intrinsic cage-only step for this client under those conditions. It does not prove an unchanged microscopic route or universal absence of chaperonin active effects.

claims.statement: At uniform concentration and constant volume, a declared reaction rate is v = νB⁻¹ dcB/dt = (dξ/dt)/V. Reaction and transport contributions are separate. An elementary reaction is one molecular step, conventionally unidirectional; a composite net reaction has no molecularity. In v = k ∏ cB^mB, the units of k depend on overall order.

limitations: The admitted primary acquisition is8.3 mM bovine pancreatic trypsin inhibitor at pH*5.2 in isotope-enriched aqueous emulsion droplets at-10 and-30 C. pH* is uncorrected for isotope effects. This is not a physiological-temperature cellular solution or an ionic-shell experiment.

SI S7 notes that the expected W111 internal-water behavior at-30 C is inconsistent with the observed dispersion. A local structural transformation causing much slower exchange is proposed but not measured; complete external-surface attribution remains conditional.

limitations: This is a synthetic DNA-origami scaffold carrying commercially supplied enzymes, not a naturally evolved protein-only multienzyme complex, living metabolic network, protein biosynthesis or a cellular-origin experiment. The scaffold DNA is supplied; its sequence-dependent assembly was not independently reconstructed.

Negatively stained TEM, dye colocalization and photobleaching report different preparations/proxies. They support source-defined loading and location, not exact atom-level interfaces, universal pair occupancy, an impermeable shell or a measured protein-protein channel.

Photobleaching copy-number estimates normalize detected Cy3 steps to labels per free enzyme and depend on labeling, detection and six-state HMM assumptions. TableS3 covers HRP, G6pDH and beta-Gal, not direct proof that every cascade cage has exactly one GOx and one HRP.

Bulk cage concentration uses A260 and an adopted extinction coefficient0.109 nM^-1cm^-1; conjugate concentrations/labeling use absorbance deconvolution and inherited coefficients. Calibration, gel-extraction losses, active-enzyme fractions and labeling are not independently reproduced.

GOx/HRP activity is a coupled ABTS absorbance readout. It depends on both enzyme steps, intermediate availability, substrate concentrations and active fractions; it is not an isolated turnover count, direct intermediate trajectory, flux control coefficient or exclusive measure of substrate transfer.

The source nominally matches enzyme/cage concentrations but paired, separately caged and uncaged preparations differ in assembly, conjugation, purification, local environment and total cage/DNA organization. No isolated geometric confinement variable or equal active-site population is proven.

Separate full cages and half-cages also increase the coupled signal. Increased activity of a co-caged pair therefore does not uniquely establish direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a proximity-only mechanism.

Hydration-layer ordering, electrostatic stabilization and conformational-substate mechanisms are proposed interpretations. Salt/helix-density comparisons alter more than one property and do not directly measure local water structure, local pH or a unique mechanism.

The single-molecule G6pDH enzymology uses a different enzyme, surface immobilization, PMS/resazurin reporter and 10 percent PEG. It is not the same GOx/HRP bulk cascade preparation or an independent replication of its fold enhancement.

The main/SI trypsin protocol annotations differ in digestion buffer, pH, enzyme concentration and assay ABTS concentration. No new protection/aggregation or persistence claim is admitted from those conflicting annotations.

No crosstalk suppression, competing-pathway insulation, local concentration gradient, intermediate residence/retention, synchronized feedback, closed metabolic cycle, sustained living-system regulation or universal efficiency benefit is measured in the admitted contexts.

limitations: Long-Evans rat hippocampus is bulk tissue containing neurons and glia. High/low licking-grooming and arched-back nursing groups are selected extremes of continuous maternal behavior, not universal biological classes.

Cross-fostering changes a postnatal care environment. General adult-age statements conflict with assay-specific 90-day descriptions. ChIP figures report four animals/group but supplementary fixed-tissue methods specify six. Exon 1_7 is an alternative first exon of the rat glucocorticoid receptor gene. CpG site 16 at the 5-prime end of the NGFI-A binding region and site 17 at its 3-prime end have different outcomes. TSA infusion is a broad pharmacological intervention, not a locus-specific methylation edit or cell-specific neural manipulation. The restraint-stress cohort is separate from the GR-protein cohort. Parallel effects do not identify their causal mediation order.

The published Figure 2-associated t/P pairs (2.1/P<0.001 and 3.1/P<0.0001) are inconsistent with ordinary t tests; exact uncertainty is not reproduced. Individual animal source values and clone sequences are unavailable in the reviewed materials. Published findings are not an independent reproduction, and nonsignificant contrasts are not equivalence tests.

limitations: Adult male 8-10-week C57BL/6-background mice; rapidly dissected bulk dentate gyri enriched in neurons, not purified neurons or single-cell measurements. ECS is induced synchronous activation, not an explicit learning task or a measured sustained cognitive state.

ATAC-seq and RNA-seq use independent samples. GEO GSE82015 lists four wild-type ATAC replicates at E0/E1/E4 and two sh-cFos E1 ATAC replicates; other AAV ATAC groups and RNA groups have three. GSE86367 lists three E24 ATAC and three RNA samples. Replicate labels do not independently verify animal identity or sample independence.

The main Methods report no sample-size predetermination, randomization or blinding. Some qPCR primer labels/sequences conflict. Published findings, metadata inspection and source-cell counts are not independent biological replication or sequencing-pipeline reproduction.

Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Marker selection, reporter maturation and a roughly 12-hour labeling window limit cell identity and temporal specificity.

Whole-hippocampus molecular samples pool nuclei across animals and neuronal subtypes. ATAC Methods specify 10,000 nuclei from 8-10 mice per replicate. Table 13 lists three Basal and four Late libraries, while the reporting summary excludes one Basal from 13 and Figure 2a states n=3 per group. The included-library mapping remains unresolved. A library, genomic locus, slice or punctum is not an independent animal. Destructive cohorts are not single-cell longitudinal measurements.

Figure 1f counts are labeled cells per DG slice; the caption refers to hippocampus. Its five versus six mice each contribute six sections, while tests report df=59/57. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. Animal-level effects and confidence intervals require source measurements and sample reconciliation.

Hi-C Methods describe two libraries per Basal, Early and Late population, but the reporting summary excludes one Early library. Methods say two animals per sample, whereas reporting specifies four to five. Promoter-capture Hi-C covers four populations and selected promoters. Contact frequencies and inferred A/B compartments are not unique three-dimensional coordinates. Figure 3 specifies a 500-kb Juicer representation, while Methods and software use 50-kb HOMER compartment PCA; their mapping needs explicit reconstruction.

ATAC Figure 2a labels log2 fold-change thresholds, while its caption, Methods and software say fold changes >1.5. RNA Table 8 has undocumented sign reorientation and a near-threshold extra row. The RNA Methods cite an edgeR reference for DESeq2 and the software omits the RNA export code. No sequence analysis, signed gene-specific pathway or edge weight is calibrated.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues. Sequencing sample sizes used observed variability and group differences; ATAC/Hi-C quality exclusions and a plotted ATAC outlier exclusion were not pre-established. Normality was assumed without formal testing. Null tests are not equivalence tests. Separate molecular profiles and behavioral outcomes do not establish a chromatin-to-memory mediation chain or lifelong persistence.

citations.note: Actually read original primary passage; source-reported preparation, observable or conditional inference only. No independent experimental replay or raw-data refit.

limitations: An E. coli B enzyme fraction, DNA, nucleotide triphosphates, divalent ions and laboratory buffer are supplied. Purification enrichment does not establish one homogeneous modern RNA-polymerase molecular complex or its subunit mechanism.

The source standard assay is a fixed incubation at 37 C; incorporation is reported as labelled nucleotide in acid-insoluble product. One labelled base does not directly report all incorporated nucleotides without a composition conversion.

Table 2 reports 7.3 millimicromoles CMP incorporation for the complete comparison and less than 0.03 after omitting DNA, enzyme or both divalent cations. These are finite omission results for that preparation, not universal absolute zeroes, microscopic rates or calibrated substrate-count thresholds.

Omission of other triphosphates suppresses the selected CMP assay, but the same publication separately reports ATP-only DNA-dependent polyadenylate formation. Therefore this assay does not prove that all four nucleotide species are universally required for every RNA product or that every DNA-dependent product is a sequence-perfect transcript.

The source product is strongly alkali-sensitive and mostly RNase-sensitive, whereas DNase does not similarly release its label. Residual RNase resistance is unresolved; no complete product sequence, unique initiation/termination mechanism or in-vivo regulatory system is measured.
The source calls supplied DNA a primer; this historical usage is not evidence that a modern covalent primer-dependent initiation mechanism has been identified.

limitations: Read the complete published primary article pages 936-947, complete PMC main HTML and all seven main figures/captions. The author-lab PDF has a graphical cover plus twelve published pages. Read selected actual 29-page publisher supplement: title page, Figure S4 page 5, Figure S7 pages 10-11, Section S2 relevant in vitro/FRAP pages 14-16, Section S6 pages 21-25, and Section S8 pages 27-28. Other SI preparation/statistical/genome-analysis pages, full sequence details, raw data and movies were not completely read.

Ddx4N1 is the supplied isolated disordered N-terminal region (residues 1-236), without the central DEAD-box helicase. Ddx4YFP replaces that helicase with YFP, and cellular/full-length constructs differ. In vitro terminal-region phase separation is not a demonstration of native germ-granule function, helicase catalysis or a universal folded-protein prerequisite.

Thermal Figure 3D reports 202 micromolar Ddx4N1, 200 mM NaCl and pH 8, with cooling/heating and same-sample repeats. Its 4 degrees C/min demonstration differs from the 2 degrees C/min default cloud-point sampling in SI Section S6. Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

Cloud-point data and Flory-Huggins/screened-Coulomb fits are separate from direct images. Assumptions about polymer volume fraction, water, effective interaction constants and electrostatic screening underlie fitted enthalpy/entropy, charge spacing and dielectric values. No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

FRAP main Figure 3C describes a 60:1 Ddx4N1:Ddx4YFP mixture; SI pages 15-16 instead list pre-dilution concentrations 292.5 micromolar Ddx4N1 and 8.1 micromolar each YFP construct and free CFP, with hanging-drop equilibration. No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

The partition experiment uses source-defined 32-base single-stranded or 32-base-paired double-stranded fluorescent DNA at equal nominal fluorophore concentration in a separate Ddx4N1 preparation. Background-subtracted emission per region volume is a concentration/partition proxy; equal quantum yield/dye behavior across phases and free-energy calibration are not independently verified.

The source defines its partition coefficient as outside/inside, not the inverse. The main Results paragraph names atto657N whereas Figure 7 and Experimental Procedures name Atto647N. No numerical partition/free-energy value, unlabeled-DNA binding constant, universal sequence specificity or corrected dye identity is independently admitted.

Ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields of view are sampling regions, not automatically sixty independent preparation replications. SD of emission regions and model-fit SE are different uncertainties. No independent replication or raw-image replay is performed.

Cellular cold/osmotic response, methylated/splice/charge/aromatic variants and genome enrichment were read but are not new admitted assay contexts. Cellular osmotic changes alter volume/concentration and environment together; sequence/general-mechanism hypotheses do not become universal proof for all condensates.

The admitted thermal, FRAP and DNA-partition contexts do not directly resolve fusion or fission dynamics, transfer/exchange rates for every component or one unique intermolecular/solvent mechanism. No direct catalytic reaction modulation, metabolic throughput/benefit, universal reaction sequestration, membrane-like selectivity, gradient maintenance, prebiotic coacervate ancestry or origin-of-life event is measured in the admitted contexts.

LC-MS records internal-standard-normalized ion counts and source-assigned lipid identities. The main text refers to PE/PG standards in Supporting Information, but the retrieved six-page supplement contains no explicit PE/PG calibration curve; no independent absolute-yield or uncertainty reconstruction is made.

Limiting-CoA conversion supports source-specific cofactor recycling, with supplied ATP and substrates. It does not close energy/resource supply, synthesize fatty-acid chains from carbon feedstock, make every phospholipid or show indefinite throughput. Small PA signal without PlsC is source-attributed to possible PlsC contamination of PlsB; omission effects are not treated as perfectly pure single-enzyme controls.

The source reports an approximate 25-30 percent expansion from R18 assumptions. No new exact area/volume expansion, vesicle number, leaflet distribution, size distribution or calibrated membrane material balance is independently admitted. Triton-normalized maximal emission is not a direct bilayer surface-area standard.

These are not matched single-vesicle samples or an interchangeable protocol. Cryo-EM snapshots are not longitudinal lineage/continuous growth tracking.

No direct leaflet-resolved synthesis, flip-flop kinetics, cation binding map, complete membrane retention, permeability/selectivity panel, electrochemical gradient or transport activity is measured here.

entities.name: Neurogenesis and cognitive preservation
entities.description: A complete neuron-birth-to-memory route remains a hypothesis. Mouse physiology and a Nestin-lineage Bax intervention constrain parts of the route; macaque histology has no matched functional assay. Rat training changes retained birth labels without isolating survival or testing newborn-cell necessity. entities.name: Nucleon valence quantum numbers
entities.description: In the declared strong-interaction nucleon sectors, net flavor means quarks minus antiquarks: proton (N_u,N_d)=(2,1), neutron (1,2), with zero other net flavors. With B=sum_f N_f/3 and Q/e=sum_f q_f*N_f, these labels give B=1 and charges +1 and 0. Adding a same-flavor quark-antiquark pair or gluons preserves these additive labels without preserving total basis-particle count.

entities.name: Fundamental color-singlet tensor
entities.description: For three fundamental SU(3) color indices, the normalized antisymmetric tensor epsilon_abc/sqrt(6) is invariant because U_ai*U_bj*U_ck*epsilon_ijk=det(U)*epsilon_abc and det(U)=1. A nontrivial center element acts as z or z^2 on one or two fundamental factors, excluding a singlet there. Three is therefore a restricted representation-theoretic minimum, not a measured particle population or sufficient formation condition.

entities.name: Nucleon Fock-sector representation
entities.description: In the specified light-front QCD framework, a proton eigenstate is expanded in quark-gluon Fock sectors with the same global quantum numbers, including uud and uudg sectors. entities.name: Physical isoscalar meson mixing

entities.name: Solar neutrino CC, NC and ES response
entities.description: In the stated solar-neutrino weak-response model, nu_e+d->p+p+e-minus is the charged-current channel, nu_x+d->p+n+nu_x is the neutral-current channel and nu_x+e-minus->nu_x+e-minus is elastic scattering. Reconstructed Cherenkov observables distinguish statistical response templates, not individually labeled incoming flavors.

entities.name: Coherent neutrino propagation in matter
entities.description: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.

sourceCoordinates.locator: 2025 review pages 10-12, Section 14.5 and Equations 14.49-14.58: coherent forward potentials, neutral matter, propagation basis and particle-sign conventions

openObligations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism, universal carrier minima or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.

entities.name: Instantaneous matter mixing and adiabatic boundary
entities.description: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. The eigenvalue gap is Delta_m/(2E), with cos(2 theta_m)=(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)/Delta_m and sin(2 theta_m)=Delta*sin(2 theta)/Delta_m. Nonzero mixing is maximal at A=Delta*cos(2 theta). An instantaneous eigenbasis has the additional connection -i*R-dagger*dR/dx; adiabatic following is an approximation that neglects its inter-state coupling relative to the gap.

entities.name: Conditional transverse two-body mass
entities.description: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

entities.name: Weak vector fields and fermion currents
entities.description: In the declared broken-phase Standard Model, W-plus and W-minus are spin-one fields of electric charge +e and -e; Z is neutral and spin one. With J_W^mu=sum_l nu-bar_l*gamma^mu*(1-gamma5)*l+sum_ij u-bar_i*gamma^mu*(1-gamma5)*V_ij*d_j, L_CC=-g/(2*sqrt(2))*(W-plus_mu*J_W^mu+h.c.). The tree neutral term is L_NC=-g/(2*cos(theta_W))*Z_mu*sum_f f-bar*gamma^mu*(gV_f-gA_f*gamma5)*f, where gV_f=T3_f-2*Q_f*sin(theta_W)^2 and gA_f=T3_f; T3_f is the isospin of the left-handed partner. Thus the stated quark charged current contains CKM mixing, while the tree Z current is flavor diagonal in this minimal mass basis.

The modified-minimal-subtraction mass mbar_q(mu_R) depends on the renormalization scale mu_R; the referenced summary table quotes u,d,s at 2 GeV and c,b at a scale equal to the respective running mass. A perturbative pole-mass prescription is distinct and has an ambiguity of order the QCD scale when related to observables.

entities.name: Quark electromagnetic current
entities.description: With e>0 the positron charge, define the quark contribution J_em,q^mu=sum_f Q_f*sum_a qbar_fa*gamma^mu*q_fa and L_em,q=-e*A_mu*J_em,q^mu. Here f labels the declared quark flavors, a is a contracted fundamental-color index, and Q_f is +2/3 for u,c,t or -1/3 for d,s,b. This electromagnetic vector current is flavor diagonal in the stated mass basis.

entities.name: Leading electromagnetic quark-parton response
entities.description: For unpolarized electromagnetic DIS in the leading massless collinear spin-one-half quark-parton model, use Q2=-q^2>0, x=Q2/(2*P.q), and F2_gamma=x*sum_f Q_f^2*(q_f+qbar_f). The flavor distributions are evaluated at the stated scale; their sum includes quarks and antiquarks rather than net valence alone. In the negligible-target-mass limit the same model gives 2*x*F1_gamma=F2_gamma, hence FL_gamma=F2_gamma-2*x*F1_gamma=0.

entities.name: Inclusive electromagnetic DIS response
entities.description: For unpolarized one-photon electron-nucleon scattering with negligible electron mass, use Q^2=4EEprime sin^2(theta/2)>0, nu=E-Eprime and x=Q^2/(2M nu). R=sigmaL/sigmaT=F2(1+4M^2*x^2/Q^2)/(2xF1)-1. The equivalent polarization convention is epsilon=[1+2(1+nu^2/Q^2)tan^2(theta/2)]^-1, Gamma=alpha*Eprime*(1/x-1)/[4*pi^2*M*E*(1-epsilon)], and Y=(d^2sigma/dOmega dEprime)/Gamma=sigmaT+epsilon*sigmaL. At fixed x,Q^2, the reduced-response intercept and slope determine R; nonzero intercept and a span in epsilon are required.

entities.name: Non-Abelian gluon self-coupling terms
entities.description: For adjoint index A=1,...,8, set K^A_mu_nu=partial_mu A^A_nu-partial_nu A^A_mu and B^A_mu_nu=f^{ABC} A^B_mu A^C_nu. The reviewed PDG convention is F=K-g_s B, so L_g=-K.K/4+(g_s/2) K.B-(g_s^2/4) B.B, with Lorentz and adjoint indices contracted. The cubic and quartic terms generate three- and four-gluon vertices proportional to g_s and g_s^2. With [t^A,t^B]=i f^{ABC}t^C and Tr(t^A t^B)=T_R delta^{AB}, fundamental SU(3) has C_F=4/3, C_A=3 and T_R=1/2.

entities.description: Confinement is specified relative to a theory and observable. In an unscreened pure-gauge theory, asymptotic fundamental Wilson-loop area behavior defines a static string-tension criterion. With dynamical quarks, the reviewed Euclidean static-source spectra instead include mixing and screening by color-singlet meson pairs. The QCD interpretation of hadronic final states is a separate phenomenological statement, not an equivalent finite-loop test or a proof that separation energy grows without bound.

Pure-gauge fundamental Wilson-loop area law, screened static-source energies with dynamical quarks and phenomenological color-singlet final states are not interchangeable definitions.

The area-law criterion takes large contours and static-source limits in an unscreened theory. Wilson strong-coupling surfaces and Creutz finite SU(2) loops do not prove continuum SU(3) confinement with physical quark masses. Their finite-volume, finite-loop and extrapolation restrictions remain explicit.

Pair creation in the reviewed dynamical-quark calculations permits color-singlet static-light or static-strange channels. The screened ground-state energy need not grow indefinitely with separation. A metastable string branch, an operator overlap and the true ground state are different quantities; Euclidean mixing energies do not measure real-time hadronization rates.

Source card 1.31 supplies possible nonperturbative formulations, including a chosen lattice action and operator basis; it is not an observed universal organization stage. Source card 1.30 supplies a renormalization prescription and scale, not physical elapsed time or a demonstrated temporal maintenance cause. Source card 1.3 supplies the non-Abelian gluon sector within QCD, not an independently measured universal maintenance arrow.

The original parent weights 0.55, 0.20 and 0.25, N_min=N_crit=1 elementary-particle counts, necessary-parent labels, TypeRole/SOMA phase placement and macro-to-micro causal story are unsupported. They have no active scientific semantics. Classification as a regime-level pattern is descriptive, not a verified universal phase sequence or material carrier.
The excluded universal downward constraint from source card 1.15 remains excluded. No intervention, closed effective dynamics or universal generating rule is established by the static-source results.

Electrical fractional-charge bounds constrain a declared material or particle search. Electric charge is not color charge; a null result cannot establish absence of all free colored objects. In particular, the CMS fractional-charge benchmark explicitly uses color-singlet particles.

Color-singlet tensor algebra is a representation constraint, not a dynamical formation proof. Asymptotic freedom concerns ultraviolet running and does not prove the infrared criterion. The high-temperature phase diagram, physical-point continuum completion and a mathematical all-channel confinement theorem are outside this admission.

No universal nuclear or atomic stability follows from the definition or the selected hadron results. Nuclear binding, decay channels and electromagnetic atomic binding require distinct systems and inputs; the existing deuteron beta threshold excludes one specified bare-nucleus breakup channel, not all decays, nuclei or atomic states.

entities.description: In the declared coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model, flavor-sensitive preparation and readout are related by interference between distinct mass propagation components. Their relative phases change transition probabilities as L/E varies; a probability is not a continuously measured sequence of flavor jumps. Oscillation is a conditional propagation phenomenon, not an additional bounded object or a universal property of every neutrino state.

This graph admits the propagation implication and explicitly excludes quantitative astrophysical transport and cosmological predictions from this reconstruction.

The spatially flat background is ds^2=dt^2-a(t)^2 dx^2, dt=a d_eta. For homogeneous phi(t), H=dot(a)/a obeys 3 M_pl^2 H^2=dot(phi)^2/2+V, dot(H)=-dot(phi)^2/(2 M_pl^2), and ddot(phi)+3H dot(phi)+V_,phi=0. The selected high-multipole sample uses 100, 143 and 217 GHz HFI half-mission cross-spectra; low-E uses the 100 x 143 GHz full-mission polarization cross-spectrum, with low-temperature Commander estimates. The low-E cleaning uses 353 GHz dust templates and a 30 GHz synchrotron template at 100 GHz. This is selection from an existing sky observation, not a new 2018 experimental preparation.

entities.name: Planck spectral response and foreground model
entities.description: Commander jointly models low-temperature foregrounds and the CMB. SimAll uses foreground-cleaned 100 x 143 GHz quasi-QML polarization estimates and simulation-based probabilities. High-multipole Plik uses masked, beam-corrected half-mission cross-spectra with noise/covariance models and foreground, calibration, polarization-efficiency and temperature-to-polarization leakage treatment. Its covariance retains correlations between frequency pairs and TT, TE and EE using a fiducial model. Cross-spectra reduce additive noise bias only insofar as the split-map noises are uncorrelated.

entities.name: Planck base-model primordial inference
entities.description: The selected analysis assumes spatially flat base LambdaCDM with purely adiabatic scalar P_R(k)=A_s*(k/k_*)^(n_s-1), k_*=0.05 Mpc^-1. CAMB (August 2017) maps this prescribed initial spectrum and the adopted background, matter and thermal history to lensed CMB spectra; CosmoMC (July 2018) samples the six-parameter posterior. The base parameters are baryon and cold-dark-matter densities, theta_MC, tau, ln(10^10 A_s) and n_s, with flat base priors; the amplitude prior is 1.61 < ln(10^10 A_s) < 3.91. The adopted neutrino model has two massless states and one 0.06 eV state, BBN-predicted helium and the stated tanh reionization history. The likelihood multiplies Commander low-T, SimAll low-E and high-multipole Plik, exploring the allowed nuisance parameters jointly.

entities.name: Regulated Wilsonian effective action
entities.description: For a well-defined regulated Euclidean real-scalar functional integral with ultraviolet momentum cutoff Lambda, split phi=phi_<+phi_> at Lambda_prime=Lambda/b with b>1. Define exp(-S_Lambda_prime[phi_<])=integral Dphi_> exp(-S_Lambda[phi_<+phi_>]), integrating only Lambda_prime<|p|<=Lambda. For sources supported below Lambda_prime, integrating the retained fields gives the same normalized low-mode generating functional as the original integral. Field-independent normalization factors cancel in that normalized functional.

entities.name: Scale flow with declared infrared direction
entities.description: After the shell step, use p_prime=b p, x_prime=x/b and a stated field normalization to restore the reference cutoff in dimensionless variables. Write the transformed action in dimensionless coupling coordinates g_i(ell), with ell=ln b and d g_i/d ell=F_i(g); increasing ell means a smaller physical cutoff Lambda_0 exp(-ell) and longer resolved lengths. Separately, a renormalized coupling g_R(mu) in a chosen subtraction scheme obeys mu d g_R/d mu=beta_R. The cutoff Lambda, subtraction scale mu and external physical momentum Q have distinct roles.

entities.name: Local fixed-point scaling classification
entities.description: For the declared infrared flow F(g), a fixed point g_* satisfies F_i(g_*)=0. Near it, d(delta g_i)/d ell=B_ij delta g_j+O(delta g^2), where B_ij=partial F_i/partial g_j at g_*. For an admitted eigen-direction with real eigenvalue y_a, its linear scaling field obeys u_a(ell)=exp(y_a ell)u_a(0). A nonredundant local operator of full fixed-point scaling dimension Delta_a coupled homogeneously in d dimensions has y_a=d-Delta_a. With ell increasing toward the infrared, y_a>0 is relevant, y_a<0 irrelevant and y_a=0 linearly marginal.

entities.name: Gaussian scalar engineering-dimension example
entities.description: For the massless Gaussian scalar kinetic action S_*=(1/2)integral d^d x (partial phi)^2 with fixed kinetic normalization, x_prime=x/b and phi_prime(x_prime)=b^((d-2)/2)phi(b x_prime) keep that term invariant. Thus [phi]_engineering=(d-2)/2 and an operator containing n fields and r derivatives has engineering dimension Delta_eng=n(d-2)/2+r. In d=4 with phi->-phi symmetry, the monomials phi^2, phi^4 and phi^6 have dimensions 2, 4 and 6, giving engineering values y=2, 0 and -2 under the stated infrared convention.

Here d is operator mass dimension, M is the heavy scale and the displayed C_i are dimensionless. With bounded coefficients and controlled loop/logarithmic corrections, finitely many operators contribute at a chosen order.

entities.name: Threshold matching and coefficient boundary data
entities.description: In the selected continuum convention use dimensional regularization with modified minimal subtraction (MSbar). At a matching scale mu_t of order M, determine EFT coefficients by equating renormalized full-theory and EFT light-particle amplitudes through the chosen momentum and loop orders, with compatible external-field and infrared conventions. At loop order n, subtract EFT contributions containing the lower-order matched coefficients from the full result; their common infrared physics cancels in a consistent matching calculation. The resulting C_i(mu_t) are boundary data; RG evolution below the threshold does not determine them without those data. A finite tree example uses J^mu=bar(e) gamma^mu (1-gamma5) nu_e and O6=J_mu^dagger J^mu, with L_eff,CC=-(G_F/sqrt(2)) O6=-g^2 O6/(8 M_W^2). Match at mu_t of order M_W for light external fermions with m_light^2 and |q^2| much smaller than M_W^2, retaining this dimension-six contact operator at tree level.

entities.name: Conditional heavy-field decoupling
entities.description: For light-particle processes below the heavy production thresholds, a consistently matched EFT can omit the heavy field as an explicit low-energy degree of freedom while retaining its virtual effects in local coefficients and renormalized light parameters. In a controlled expansion with light scales E much smaller than M and non-growing dimensionless matching coefficients, higher-dimensional contributions are suppressed by powers of E/M. This conditional suppression does not erase heavy-field effects in the relevant or marginal sector.

entities.name: Two-dimensional hard-disk equilibrium model
entities.description: The selected model contains N structureless disks of radius sigma in a two-dimensional periodic square of area V=L^2, with packing fraction eta=N*pi*sigma^2/V. Nonoverlapping configurations have zero potential energy and overlaps are forbidden. At fixed packing fraction its equilibrium phase behavior is independent of temperature, while pressure is proportional to temperature. Dense ordering can therefore be entropic without an attractive pair potential. Local sixfold bond orientation is Psi_k=average_l exp(6*i*phi_kl), with neighbors supplied by the stated construction, and sample orientation is Psi=N^-1*sum_k Psi_k.

entities.name: Finite icosahedral Al-Mn order and reported metastability
entities.description: For the selected rapidly cooled Al-Mn material, the source reports sharp electron diffraction with six fivefold, ten threefold and fifteen twofold axes of an icosahedral point group, with orientational correlation across finite grains up to about 2 micrometers. entities.name: Entropic hard-disk ordering and distinct transitions
entities.description: The reported two-dimensional hard-disk calculations support first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence over approximately eta=0.700 to 0.716, using coexistence patterns, the equilibrium equation of state and interface scaling. At eta=0.718 the source finds exponential positional decay on a scale of about 100 disk radii and very slow orientational decay, interpreted as a single hexatic phase. Near eta=0.720 the positional correlations become approximately algebraic, near r^-1/3 over the resolved range, and the source identifies a continuous hexatic-solid transition. Thus this specified entropic model has ordered regimes and two distinct transition characters.

entities.name: Finite-sphere screened repulsive pair model

This is a screened repulsive pair term, with finite-sphere amplitude and an effective charge that need not equal titratable charge.

entities.description: For the declared isothermal uniform bulk linear response, the proper piezoelectric stress tensor is e_ijk=(partial D_i/partial strain_jk) at fixed E,T, equivalently -(partial stress_jk/partial E_i) at fixed strain,T. Its SI units are C/m^2. The piezoelectric strain tensor d relates strain to electric field at fixed stress,T or displacement D to stress at fixed E,T, with units m/V, equivalently C/N. Converting between e and d requires elastic compliance and matching tensor/shear conventions; they are not interchangeable numerical coefficients.

entities.name: Bound-body recoil and zero-phonon nuclear transition
entities.description: For a free nucleus of mass M, the leading nonrelativistic recoil energy is E_R=E_gamma^2/(2*M*c^2), displacing emission below and absorption above the nuclear transition energy. In the selected bound-solid oscillator account, a recoilless nuclear gamma event leaves the internal vibrational occupation state unchanged. Momentum is still transferred to the bound body; its whole-body translational recoil energy is negligibly small on the stated spectral scale. This zero-phonon channel is a fraction of events, not absence of binding vibrations, zero momentum transfer or a rule that every emitted gamma ray is resonant.

entities.name: Orbital electron capture and charge-state boundary
entities.description: Orbital electron capture consumes a bound electron in a specified nuclear transition and emits an electron neutrino; in the selected 140Pr to 140Ce channel it converts a proton to a neutron, preserves mass number A=140 and lowers nuclear charge Z from 59 to 58. Initial bare 140Pr59+, hydrogenlike 140Pr58+ and heliumlike 140Pr57+ carry zero, one and two bound electrons respectively. EC removes one bound electron while lowering Z by one, so the daughter ionic charge remains the same. Changing the initial ionization state does not change which parent isotope is prepared; the subsequent nuclear decay does change the element.

entities.name: Declared linear homogeneous optical-propagation model
entities.description: In the selected homogeneous isotropic linear medium, use the convention E(z,t)=Re[E0(omega)*exp(i*k(omega)*z-i*omega*t)] with k(omega)=omega*sqrt(epsilon(omega)*mu(omega)) in absolute SI constitutive units. Writing k=k_real+i*k_imag gives amplitude attenuation exp(-k_imag*z) and phase accumulation k_real*z. For the passive forward branch, k_imag>=0; the corresponding fixed-medium intensity attenuation coefficient is alpha_int=2*k_imag in m^-1. Nonlinear real propagation phase across a pulse bandwidth can produce dispersive waveform deformation, whereas a real phase linear in frequency supplies a delay. A wave number proportional to frequency at fixed speed is not by itself dispersive deformation. These phase effects are distinct from imaginary-part attenuation.

entities.name: Conditional KSI mutation and solvation interpretation
entities.description: Combining the variant turnover losses, Y16S/D40N analogue geometry and fluorophenolate solvent comparisons, Kraut and colleagues propose that smaller residue 16 substitutions allow cavity water to mitigate loss of the Tyr donor, whereas Phe16 adds unfavorable desolvation beyond removing the Tyr hydrogen bond. entities.name: Defined-substrate lysate degradation context
entities.description: Engineer N-end-rule-tagged E. coli DHFR/cpLys38, selected C-terminally tagged cpLys38, lysine-less unstructured-tail additions, terminal His6 and linear Ub4 variants as defined in Figures 2-5. cpLys38 joins the old termini with six glycines and starts at former Lys38/ends at Asn37.
